window.text: In US cohorts of DES-exposed sons, undescended testis, epididymal cysts and testicular inflammation were more strongly associated with exposure before the 11th week of gestation, though timing could not be definitively separated from dose.
window.quote: Because nearly all women who receive a cumulative dose of 5 grams or greater had begun taking DES before the 11th week of gestation, it was not possible to determine definitively which of these factors was more important.
window.source_label: Palmer JR et al. Urogenital abnormalities in men exposed to diethylstilbestrol in utero: a cohort study (three pooled US cohorts, 1,197 exposed, 1,038 unexposed). Environ Health 2009;8:37, open-access full text, Results (Table 2) and Discussion

dose.text: In the US DESAD cohort, cervical and vaginal structural anomalies in daughters were closely associated with the total DES dose and the gestational week of first exposure; the abstract gives no threshold.
dose.quote: Among the 367 cases found by record review to have complete information on the DES exposure, multivariate analysis indicated close association of the anomalies with the gestational week of first exposure and the total dose.
dose.source_label: Jefferies JA et al. Structural anomalies of the cervix and vagina in women enrolled in the Diethylstilbestrol Adenosis (DESAD) Project. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1984;148(1):59-66, PubMed abstract

effects.text: US FDA-approved estrogen labelling states that DES-exposed daughters have increased risks of vaginal adenosis, cervical squamous dysplasia and clear-cell vaginal cancer later in life, and sons of urogenital abnormalities and possibly testicular cancer.
effects.quote: female offspring have an increased risk of vaginal adenosis, squamous cell dysplasia of the uterine cervix, and clear cell vaginal cancer later in life; male offspring have an increased risk of urogenital abnormalities and possibly testicular cancer
effects.source_label: US FDA-approved labeling (ANDA040312), Innofem estradiol tablets USP, boxed warning on estrogens in pregnancy, DailyMed, revised 4/2017 (product marketing ended 2009)

absolute_risk.text: In the US DESAD cohort, structural anomalies of the cervix or vagina were found in 25% of 1,655 DES-exposed daughters identified from prenatal records, versus 2% of 963 control subjects.
absolute_risk.quote: 25% of the 1,655 subjects identified by review of prenatal records, 43% of the 800 who themselves requested entry into the project, and 49% of the 1,089 referred by physicians but in only 2% of the 963 control subjects.
absolute_risk.source_label: Jefferies JA et al. Structural anomalies of the cervix and vagina in women enrolled in the Diethylstilbestrol Adenosis (DESAD) Project. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1984;148(1):59-66, PubMed abstract

paternal.text: France's medicines agency states that, to date, no consequences have been shown in children whose fathers were themselves exposed to DES before birth.
paternal.quote: À ce jour, il n’a pas été mis en évidence de conséquences chez les enfants de pères exposés in utero au DES.
paternal.source_label: ANSM (French medicines agency), dossier thématique 'Diéthylstilbestrol (DES) et grossesse', published 20/07/2026, updated 21/07/2026

other_effects.text: Women exposed to DES before birth had higher cumulative risks than unexposed women of infertility (33.3% vs 15.5%), spontaneous abortion (50.3% vs 38.6%) and preterm delivery (53.3% vs 17.8%), assessed to age 45.
other_effects.quote: for infertility, 33.3% vs. 15.5% (hazard ratio, 2.37; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.05 to 2.75); spontaneous abortion, 50.3% vs. 38.6% (hazard ratio, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.42 to 1.88); preterm delivery, 53.3% vs. 17.8%
other_effects.source_label: Hoover RN et al. Adverse health outcomes in women exposed in utero to diethylstilbestrol (three pooled studies initiated in the 1970s). N Engl J Med 2011;365(14):1304-14, PubMed abstract, Results

regulatory.text: In France, the indication for recurrent spontaneous miscarriage was removed in 1976 and a contraindication for use in pregnant women was added in 1977.
regulatory.quote: En France, l’indication " avortements spontanés à répétition " a été supprimée en 1976 et la contre-indication d’utilisation chez la femme enceinte a été ajoutée en 1977.
regulatory.source_label: Afssaps (now ANSM), Mise au point 'Complications liées à l’exposition in utero au diéthylstilbestrol (DES)', Actualisation 2011 (June 2011), Historique

monitoring.text: For women exposed to DES before birth, France's medicines agency recommends reinforced gynaecological follow-up for dysplasia, adenosis and adenocarcinoma, plus breast cancer screening as recommended for their age.
monitoring.quote: Suivi gynécologique renforcé (dysplasie, adénose, adénocarcinome). Dépistage du cancer du sein selon les recommandations pour cette tranche d’âge.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM (French medicines agency), dossier thématique 'Diéthylstilbestrol (DES) et grossesse', section Pour les professionnels de santé, Prise en charge, 2e génération, published 20/07/2026, updated 21/07/2026

evidence_base.text: Human evidence includes the pooled long-term follow-up of three studies started in the 1970s, covering 4,653 women exposed to DES before birth and 1,927 unexposed controls.
evidence_base.quote: We combined data from three studies initiated in the 1970s with continued long-term follow-up of 4653 women exposed in utero to DES and 1927 unexposed controls.

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC N03AB02).

window.text: The French product information says a particular syndrome is suggested with hydantoin use, such as phenytoin, in the first trimester; it gives no window in weeks.
window.quote: Un syndrome particulier est évoqué pour la prise d'hydantoïnes au premier trimestre.
window.source_label: ANSM, DI-HYDAN 100 mg (phenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

dose.text: The UK medicines regulator judged the data on dose inconsistent and too limited to conclude whether phenytoin's malformation risk depends on dose.
dose.quote: Overall, these data are inconsistent and too limited to draw conclusions on a dose-dependent risk of congenital malformations following phenytoin exposure in utero.
dose.source_label: MHRA / Commission on Human Medicines, Public Assessment Report: antiepileptic drugs, review of safety of use during pregnancy, section 3.7

effects.text: The US label says more major malformations, such as clefts and heart defects, and fetal hydantoin syndrome features, including nail and digit hypoplasia, microcephaly and cognitive deficits, have been reported.
effects.quote: Increased frequencies of major malformations (such as orofacial clefts and cardiac defects), and abnormalities characteristic of fetal hydantoin syndrome, including dysmorphic skull and facial features, nail and digit hypoplasia, growth abnormalities (including microcephaly), and cognitive deficits, have been reported
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Dilantin Infatabs (phenytoin), Pfizer, section 5.13 (via openFDA)

absolute_risk.text: The UK medicines regulator says the data support that around 6 in 100 children exposed to phenytoin alone in pregnancy have a malformation, against 2 to 3 in 100 generally.
absolute_risk.quote: around 6% of children exposed to phenytoin monotherapy during pregnancy suffer from congenital malformations; this risk is increased compared with that in children of mothers who were not exposed to antiepileptics during pregnancy (2-3% in the general population)
absolute_risk.source_label: MHRA / Commission on Human Medicines, Public Assessment Report: antiepileptic drugs, review of safety of use during pregnancy, key findings for phenytoin

before_after.text: EU regulators say a pregnancy test should be considered before starting oral phenytoin, and women who could become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Pregnancy testing in women of childbearing potential should be considered prior to initiating treatment with X. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping treatment.
before_after.source_label: EMA/CMDh, phenytoin PSUSA: scientific conclusions and amendments to the product information, Annex II, SmPC section 4.6 (oral phenytoin products)

other_effects.text: The UK regulator says that, although clinical studies report inconsistent findings, the totality of the data shows a possible adverse effect of phenytoin on the child's neurodevelopment.
other_effects.quote: for phenobarbital and phenytoin, although the clinical studies report inconsistent findings, the totality of the data show the possibility of adverse effects on neurodevelopment
other_effects.source_label: MHRA, Drug Safety Update vol. 14 issue 6: Antiepileptic drugs in pregnancy, updated advice following comprehensive safety review

regulatory.text: Under a 2021 EU agreement, oral phenytoin product information says it should not be used in women of childbearing potential unless, after careful consideration of alternatives, the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks.
regulatory.quote: X should not be used in women of childbearing potential unless the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks following careful consideration of alternative suitable treatment options.
regulatory.source_label: EMA/CMDh, phenytoin PSUSA: CMDh position (agreement adopted at the April 2021 CMDh meeting), Annex II, SmPC section 4.4 (oral phenytoin products)

monitoring.text: If phenytoin must continue in pregnancy, the French product information requires specialised prenatal monitoring aimed at the described malformations, with the same screening whether or not the woman took folic acid.
monitoring.quote: une surveillance prénatale spécialisée orientée sur les malformations décrites ci-dessus doit être instaurée. Le dépistage des malformations sera identique que la patiente ait reçu ou non de l'acide folique.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, DI-HYDAN 100 mg (phenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

evidence_base.text: The UK regulator's review rests on clinical studies, including meta-analyses and pregnancy registries, of more than 2,000 phenytoin-exposed pregnancies, around 1,000 of them exposed in the first trimester.
evidence_base.quote: Clinical studies involving more than 2,000 pregnancies exposed to phenytoin, including around 1,000 pregnancies exposed in the first trimester, show an increased risk of major congenital malformations following prenatal phenytoin exposure
evidence_base.source_label: MHRA / Commission on Human Medicines, Public Assessment Report: antiepileptic drugs, review of safety of use during pregnancy, section 3.7

regulatory.text: French ANSM minocycline product information contraindicates cyclines from the second trimester and, as a precaution, prefers that they not be used in the first trimester.
regulatory.quote: par mesure de précaution, il est préférable de ne pas utiliser les cyclines pendant le premier trimestre de la grossesse. A partir du deuxième trimestre de la grossesse, l'administration de cyclines est contre-indiquée.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, MYNOCINE 100 mg gélule (minocycline), RCP section 4.6

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

regulatory.text: French ANSM minocycline product information contraindicates cyclines from the second trimester and, as a precaution, prefers that they not be used in the first trimester.
regulatory.quote: par mesure de précaution, il est préférable de ne pas utiliser les cyclines pendant le premier trimestre de la grossesse. A partir du deuxième trimestre de la grossesse, l'administration de cyclines est contre-indiquée.

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

regulatory.text: Japan's Tigason label opens with a warning that etretinate is teratogenic and must not be given to pregnant women or to women who may be pregnant.
regulatory.quote: 本剤には催夺形性があるので、姊婦又は姊娠している可能性のある女性には投与しないこと。
regulatory.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 1 Warning

effects.text: The US acitretin label lists fetal abnormalities reported with acitretin and/or etretinate, including meningomyelocele, facial dysmorphia, syndactyly, absent terminal phalanges and malformations of hip, ankle and forearm.
effects.quote: Major human fetal abnormalities associated with acitretin and/or etretinate administration have been reported including meningomyelocele; meningoencephalocele; multiple synostoses; facial dysmorphia; syndactyly; absence of terminal phalanges; malformations of hip, ankle, and forearm
effects.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

other_effects.text: For conceptions after the last etretinate or acitretin dose, the US label lists reported abnormal outcomes including premature birth, neonatal apnoea or anaemia, hypotonia and hypocalcaemia, without judging retinoid causation.
other_effects.quote: 15 of the outcomes were abnormal (including cases of absent hand/wrist, clubfoot, GI malformation, hypocalcemia, hypotonia, limb malformation, neonatal apnea/anemia, neonatal ichthyosis, placental disorder/death, undescended testicle, and 5 cases of premature birth)
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

before_after.text: Japan's label says a woman who could become pregnant and must take etretinate has to use contraception during treatment and for at least 2 years after stopping.
before_after.quote: 姊娠する可能性のある女性で他に代わるべき治療法がない重症な患者にやむを得ず投与する場合には、投与中及び投与中止後少なくとも２年間は避姊させること。
before_after.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 8.2.2

paternal.text: Japan's label, citing animal (guinea pig) reports of abnormal sperm formation, tells men taking etretinate to use contraception during treatment and for at least 6 months after stopping.
paternal.quote: 本剤はモルモットを用いた動物実験で、精子形成能に異常を起こすことが報告されているので男性に投与する場合には、投与中及び投与中止後少なくとも６ヶ月間は避姊させること。
paternal.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 8.2.3

evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

dose.text: In rat studies, fingolimod was teratogenic at 0.1 mg/kg or higher, where drug exposure was similar to that of patients on the 0.5 mg therapeutic dose.

effects.text: The US label says the most frequent major birth defects in the Gilenya pregnancy registry were congenital heart defects, renal/urinary malformations and limb/musculoskeletal malformations.
effects.quote: The most frequent major birth defects were congenital heart defects, renal/urinary malformations, and limb/musculoskeletal malformations.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data

other_effects.text: In rats given fingolimod during pregnancy and lactation, pup survival fell at all doses and offspring showed a learning deficit at the high dose (animal data).
other_effects.quote: pup survival was decreased at all doses and a neurobehavioral (learning) deficit was seen in offspring at the high dose
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data

absolute_risk.text: In the Gilenya pregnancy registry (2011-2024), 8.2% (EUROCAT) or 10.9% (MACDP) of 147 first-trimester-exposed outcomes had major birth defects, against a 2% to 4% US background.
absolute_risk.quote: the rate of major birth defects among 147 live births, stillbirths, or terminations of pregnancy due to fetal anomalies from women who were administered fingolimod during the first trimester was 8.2% (95% CI: 4.3-13.8)
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data (Gilenya Pregnancy Registry 2011-2024)

before_after.text: EU product information requires a negative pregnancy test before starting, effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after stopping, and stopping fingolimod 2 months before planning a pregnancy.
before_after.quote: Women of childbearing potential must use effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after discontinuation of Gilenya, since fingolimod takes approximately 2 months to eliminate from the body after treatment discontinuation
before_after.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, sections 4.4 and 4.6

paternal.text: Health Canada says available data do not suggest that fingolimod is associated with an increased risk of male-mediated fetal toxicity.
paternal.quote: Available data do not suggest that GILENYA would be associated with an increased risk of male-mediated fetal toxicity.
paternal.source_label: Health Canada, GILENYA Product Monograph (Novartis), authorized 2 September 2026, section 7 Reproductive Health, Male Reproductive Toxicity

monitoring.text: EU product information says to stop fingolimod if a woman becomes pregnant, give medical advice on the fetal risk, and perform ultrasonography examinations.
monitoring.quote: Medical advice should be given regarding the risk of harmful effects to the foetus associated with treatment and ultrasonography examinations should be performed.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, section 4.6 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: The 2019 EU review that found a two-fold malformation risk used post-marketing data, including registry data, with prospective data from 1,465 women exposed to fingolimod during pregnancy.

effects.text: A 2013 US NTP systematic review suggests a possible pattern of craniofacial and skeletal malformations after first-trimester fluorouracil exposure, usually absent or fused fingers or toes.
effects.quote: There may be a pattern of craniofacial and/or skeletal malformations, usually involving the absence or fusion of the digits of the hand and/or foot, following first-trimester exposure
effects.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

other_effects.text: In the final 2013 NTP systematic review, 129 infants exposed to fluorouracil before birth were followed for 6 weeks to 17 years, and growth and development were normal in all but 4.
other_effects.quote: Normal growth and development were reported for all but 4 children.
other_effects.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

absolute_risk.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review reports an apparent rate of major malformations likely attributable to first-trimester fluorouracil exposure of 31% (4/13) in published cases, against 3% in the US general population.
absolute_risk.quote: the apparent rate of major malformations likely attributable to exposure to 5-fluorouracil in the first trimester was 31% (4/13 conceptuses, based on 10 liveborn infants and examination of the fetuses of 2 induced abortions and 1 stillbirth)
absolute_risk.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.4 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

before_after.text: Health Canada recommends a pregnancy test before starting intravenous fluorouracil and effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.
before_after.quote: An effective method of contraception should be used during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose of 5-fluorouracil.
before_after.source_label: Health Canada product monograph, Fluorouracil Injection USP (Accord Healthcare), sections 2 and 7

paternal.text: The US label says fluorouracil may damage sperm and advises men with partners who could become pregnant to use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after stopping.
paternal.quote: Fluorouracil may damage spermatozoa. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and for 3 months following cessation of therapy with fluorouracil
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Fluorouracil Injection (Fresenius Kabi, ANDA040278), section 8.6, via openFDA

monitoring.text: After accidental use of Efudix cream in pregnancy, French product information says to stop treatment and follow the pregnancy with targeted prenatal monitoring, without systematically advising termination.
monitoring.quote: En cas d’administration accidentelle pendant la grossesse, le traitement doit être interrompu.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, EFUDIX 5% crème RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

evidence_base.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review documents 178 fluorouracil-exposed pregnancies from published reports in cancer patients, 17 of them in the first trimester and 172 on polytherapy.
evidence_base.quote: In utero exposure to 5-fluorouracil was documented for 178 pregnancies, including 1 twin pregnancy (179 conceptuses)
evidence_base.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC G03BA01).

regulatory.text: The US testosterone enanthate label, like the other US androgen labels read, contraindicates androgens in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.quote: Androgens are contraindicated in men with carcinomas of the breast or with known or suspected carcinomas of the prostate and in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

window.text: The US label, counting by trimester, says masculinisation of a female fetus is most likely when androgens are given in the first trimester, and its degree is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus.
window.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus and is most likely to occur in the female fetus when the drugs are given in the first trimester.
window.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

dose.text: The US methyltestosterone label says the degree of masculinisation is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus, and it states no threshold dose.
dose.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and age of the fetus
dose.source_label: US label, Methitest (methyltestosterone) tablets, Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, Contraindications, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says androgens given in pregnancy virilise the external genitals of a female fetus, with clitoral enlargement, abnormal vaginal development and genital folds fused into a scrotum-like structure.
effects.quote: When administered to pregnant women, androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus. This virilization includes clitoromegaly, abnormal vaginal development, and fusion of genital folds to form a scrotal-like structure.
effects.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

other_effects.text: In animal studies, the US Xyosted label says testosterone exposure in the womb caused hormonal and behavioural changes in offspring as well as structural impairments of reproductive tissues in both sexes.
other_effects.quote: In animal developmental studies, exposure to testosterone in utero resulted in hormonal and behavioral changes in offspring and structural impairments of reproductive tissues in female and male offspring.
other_effects.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

paternal.text: France's ANSM says pregnant women must avoid all contact with testosterone gel application sites, and a man whose partner is pregnant must be especially careful with the precautions against transfer.
paternal.quote: Les femmes enceintes doivent éviter tout contact avec les sites d'application de ce médicament. En cas de grossesse chez sa partenaire, le patient devra être d'autant plus vigilant quant aux précautions d'utilisation
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Androgel 50 mg gel transdermique en sachet-dose, RCP section 4.4 (Transfert peau à peau)

monitoring.text: The US label says a patient who becomes pregnant while taking androgens should be told of the potential hazard to the fetus, and it names no specific prenatal test or newborn check.
monitoring.quote: If the patient becomes pregnant while taking androgens, she should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The Xyosted label bases the statement that testosterone is teratogenic on animal data and its mechanism of action, and it gives no count of exposed human pregnancies.
evidence_base.quote: Testosterone is teratogenic and may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman based on data from animal studies and its mechanism of action
evidence_base.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

entries.name: Fosphenytoin

sources.label: ENTIS expert list of known human structural teratogens
sources.note: Fosphenytoin is on the list of medicines that ENTIS experts identify as known human structural teratogens (Bluett-Duncan M et al. A Scoping Review of Human Teratogens and Their Impact on the Developing Brain. Birth Defects Res. 2025;117(9):e2497).

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

effects.text: The US fosphenytoin label says more major malformations, such as clefts and heart defects, and fetal hydantoin syndrome features, including nail and digit hypoplasia, have been reported with phenytoin, its active metabolite.
effects.quote: Increased frequencies of major malformations (such as orofacial clefts and cardiac defects), and abnormalities characteristic of fetal hydantoin syndrome, including dysmorphic skull and facial features, nail and digit hypoplasia, growth abnormalities (including microcephaly), and cognitive deficits, have been reported
effects.source_label: US FDA label, CEREBYX (fosphenytoin sodium), Pfizer, section 5.15 (via openFDA)

absolute_risk.text: The French fosphenytoin product information says phenytoin exposure in pregnancy is associated with a major malformation rate 2 to 3 times higher than the general population's rate of 2 to 3 in 100.
absolute_risk.quote: l’exposition à la phénytoïne au cours de la grossesse est associée à une fréquence de malformations majeures 2 à 3 fois plus élevée que celle de la population générale, dont la fréquence est de 2 à 3 %
absolute_risk.source_label: ANSM, PRODILANTIN 75 mg/mL (fosphenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

before_after.text: The French fosphenytoin product information says women of childbearing potential must use effective contraception during treatment, and a pregnancy test should be considered before starting.
before_after.quote: Les femmes en âge de procréer doivent utiliser une méthode contraceptive efficace pendant le traitement. Une recherche de grossesse doit être envisagée chez les femmes en âge de procréer avant l’instauration d’un traitement par PRODILANTIN.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, PRODILANTIN 75 mg/mL (fosphenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

other_effects.text: The French fosphenytoin product information says studies of neurodevelopmental risk in children exposed to phenytoin during pregnancy are contradictory and the risk cannot be excluded.
other_effects.quote: Les études liées au risque neurodéveloppemental chez les enfants exposés à la phénytoïne pendant la grossesse sont contradictoires et le risque ne peut être exclu.
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, PRODILANTIN 75 mg/mL (fosphenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

regulatory.text: The French fosphenytoin (PRODILANTIN) product information says it must not be used in women of childbearing potential, women planning a pregnancy or pregnant women, except in case of clinical need.
regulatory.quote: PRODILANTIN ne doit pas être utilisé chez les femmes en âge de procréer, les femmes qui planifient une grossesse et les femmes enceintes, sauf en cas de besoin clinique.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, PRODILANTIN 75 mg/mL (fosphenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

monitoring.text: If fosphenytoin is continued in pregnancy after careful benefit-risk reassessment, the French product information recommends the lowest effective dose and an adapted prenatal follow-up aimed at the described malformations.
monitoring.quote: Si après réévaluation attentive du bénéfice/risque, le traitement par PRODILANTIN est poursuivi pendant la grossesse, il est recommandé d'utiliser la dose minimale efficace et d’instaurer un suivi prénatal adapté, orienté sur la survenue éventuelle des malformations décrites.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, PRODILANTIN 75 mg/mL (fosphenytoin) RCP, section 4.6

evidence_base.text: The US fosphenytoin label takes its human evidence from phenytoin, the active metabolite, citing meta-analyses of observational studies and registries that estimate an approximately 2.4-fold increased risk of any major malformation.
evidence_base.quote: Meta-analyses using data from published observational studies and registries have estimated an approximately 2.4-fold increased risk for any major malformation in children with prenatal phenytoin exposure compared to controls.
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, CEREBYX (fosphenytoin sodium), Pfizer, section 8.1 (via openFDA)

regulatory.quote: HICON ® is contraindicated in pregnancy because sodium iodide I 131 crosses the placenta and fetal exposure can lead to neonatal hypothyroidism.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

window.text: The fetal thyroid begins to concentrate iodide during the 10th to 12th week of gestation; the label does not state whether weeks count from conception or the last period.
window.quote: Sodium iodide I 131 crosses the placenta and the fetal thyroid begins to concentrate iodide during the 10 th to 12 th week of gestation.
window.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

dose.text: In literature reports of maternal doses of 333 to 8,325 MBq (9 to 225 mCi) at 4 to 26 weeks gestational age, the most common adverse outcome was hypothyroidism in infants and children.
dose.quote: maternal exposures to sodium iodide I 131 at doses of 333 MBq to 8,325 MBq (9 mCi to 225 mCi) during 4 to 26 weeks gestational age, the most common adverse outcomes were hypothyroid infants and children
dose.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

effects.text: Published reports describe neonatal thyroid abnormalities after fetal exposure, including thyroid agenesis (absent thyroid) and hypothyroidism.
effects.quote: Data from the published literature describe reports of neonatal thyroid abnormalities after fetal exposure; including agenesis of the thyroid and hypothyroidism
effects.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

other_effects.text: Late diagnosis of neonatal hypothyroidism after in utero exposure can lead to severe sequelae such as cognitive impairment and delayed bone age.
other_effects.quote: Delay in diagnosis of neonatal hypothyroidism after exposure to sodium iodide I 131 in utero can result in severe sequelae such as cognitive impairment and delayed bone age.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: In a Korean cohort of treated thyroid-cancer patients, malformation rates were 13.3% when conception occurred 0 to 5 months after radioiodine, against 7.9%, 8.3% and 9.6% for later intervals.
absolute_risk.quote: congenital malformation rates of 13.3% for the interval of 0 to 5 months, 7.9% for 6 to 11 months, 8.3% for 12 to 23 months, and 9.6% for 24 months or more
absolute_risk.source_label: Kim HO et al., Pregnancy outcomes and radioactive iodine treatment after thyroidectomy among women with thyroid cancer, JAMA Intern Med 2020 (Korean nationwide cohort)

before_after.text: The French SmPC requires effective contraception in men and women until 6 months after treatment of benign disease and until 12 months after treatment of thyroid cancer.
before_after.quote: une contraception efficace sera mise en place et maintenue chez l'homme et la femme jusqu'à 6 mois après traitement d'une affection bénigne et jusqu'à 12 mois après traitement d'un cancer thyroïdien
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP Iodure (131 I) de sodium pour therapie Curiumpharma 37-7 400 MBq, gelule

paternal.text: The French SmPC advises men treated with radioiodine to wait 6 to 12 months before fathering a child, so that irradiated sperm are replaced.
paternal.quote: Il doit être recommandé aux hommes traités par l'iode radioactif d'attendre 6 à 12 mois avant de procréer, le temps que les spermatozoïdes irradiés soient remplacés par des non irradiés.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, RCP Iodure (131 I) de sodium pour therapie Curiumpharma 37-7 400 MBq, gelule

monitoring.text: The US label says to monitor thyroid function in any infant born after in utero exposure to sodium iodide I-131.
monitoring.quote: Monitor thyroid function in any infant born after in utero exposure to sodium iodide I 131.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

evidence_base.text: For conception after thyroid-cancer treatment, a meta-analysis of seven observational studies with 13,811 pregnancies found no significant effect on congenital malformation (OR 1.00).
evidence_base.quote: Seven observational studies were eligible, involving 125,591 participants and 13,811 pregnancies.
evidence_base.source_label: Zhang L et al., The effect of I-131 therapy on pregnancy outcomes after thyroidectomy in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: a meta-analysis, Endocrine 2021

sources.mechanism: State's Qualified Experts

California (USA).enforcement: Attorney General, district attorneys and private enforcers; civil penalties up to USD 2,500 per violation per day.

jurisdictions.EU / EEA: Authorised with a pregnancy prevention programme; contraindicated in pregnancy.
jurisdictions.USA: Isotretinoin authorised under the iPLEDGE REMS programme.

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC D10AD04, D10BA01).

window.text: The US label names no gestational week and says that potentially any fetus exposed during pregnancy can be affected.
window.quote: Potentially any fetus exposed during pregnancy can be affected. There are no accurate means of determining prenatally whether an exposed fetus has been affected.
window.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), boxed warning and section 5.1, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

dose.text: The US label says the risk of life-threatening birth defects is extremely high if pregnancy occurs while taking any amount, even for short periods.
dose.quote: There is an extremely high risk that life-threatening birth defects will result if pregnancy occurs while taking any amount of ABSORICA/ABSORICA LD even for short periods of time.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 5.1, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

effects.text: The US label lists malformations of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, heart and blood vessels, and thymus and parathyroid glands, but not limb defects.
effects.quote: Major congenital malformations that have been documented following isotretinoin exposure include malformations of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 8.1 human data, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

absolute_risk.text: The EMA's safety committee says human data show a risk of retinoid embryopathy in up to 30% of exposed fetuses, for oral retinoids as a group, without a comparison rate.
absolute_risk.quote: The human data on congenital malformations after oral retinoid exposure shows a significant risk of retinoid embryopathy (of up to 30% of fetuses exposed)
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA PRAC assessment report, Article 31 referral on retinoid-containing medicinal products, section 3 benefit-risk balance

before_after.text: The French label requires contraception from at least 1 month before isotretinoin, throughout treatment and for at least 1 month after stopping, even in women without periods.
before_after.quote: Une méthode de contraception doit être utilisée pendant au moins 1 mois avant le début du traitement, pendant toute la durée du traitement et pendant au moins 1 mois après l'arrêt du traitement par l’isotrétinoïne, même en cas d’aménorrhée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.4 (Programme de Prévention de la Grossesse, Contraception), RCP updated 30/07/2026

paternal.text: The French label says available data suggest that maternal exposure through the semen of men taking isotretinoin is too low to be linked to the drug's teratogenic effects.
paternal.quote: Les données disponibles suggèrent que le niveau d'exposition maternelle à partir du sperme des patients traités par ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle n’est pas suffisant pour être associé aux effets tératogènes d’ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.4 (Hommes), RCP updated 30/07/2026

other_effects.text: The US label reports cases of IQ below 85, with or without other abnormalities, in children exposed before birth, and an increased risk of miscarriage and premature birth.
other_effects.quote: Cases of IQ scores less than 85 with or without other abnormalities have been reported in children exposed in utero to isotretinoin. An increased risk of spontaneous abortion and premature births have been reported with isotretinoin exposure during pregnancy.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA (SPL version 21)

regulatory.text: The French label contraindicates isotretinoin in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and in women who could become pregnant unless every condition of the Pregnancy Prevention Programme is met.
regulatory.quote: L'isotrétinoïne est contre-indiquée chez les femmes enceintes ou qui allaitent (voir rubrique 4.6). L'isotrétinoïne est contre-indiquée chez les femmes en âge de procréer sauf si toutes les conditions du « Programme de Prévention de la Grossesse » sont remplies
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.3 Contre-indications, RCP updated 30/07/2026

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs, the US label says to stop isotretinoin immediately and refer to an obstetrician-gynaecologist experienced in reproductive toxicity, and that no accurate means can determine prenatally whether an exposed fetus is affected.
monitoring.quote: There are no accurate means of determining prenatally whether an exposed fetus has been affected. If pregnancy occurs, discontinue ABSORICA/ABSORICA LD immediately and refer the patient to an Obstetrician- Gynecologist experienced in reproductive toxicity for further evaluation and counseling
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), boxed warning, via openFDA (SPL version 21)

evidence_base.text: A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies with 2,783 isotretinoin-exposed women found a 15% sample-weighted major-malformation rate, and only 3 studies had an unexposed comparison group.
evidence_base.quote: Ten eligible studies that combined 2,783 isotretinoin-exposed women were included in our study. The rate of MM weighted for the sample size was 15%. Three studies that included an unexposed comparison group were eligible for the meta-analysis.
evidence_base.source_label: Choi et al., The rates of major malformations after gestational exposure to isotretinoin: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Obstet Gynecol Sci 2021;64(4):364-373 (abstract)

sources.label: EFSA health-based guidance value
sources.note: Lead: No tolerable intake set; reference point 0.5 µg per kg of body weight per day for developmental neurotoxicity. EFSA concluded in its 2010 opinion on lead in food that the provisional tolerable weekly intake of 25 µg per kg of body weight was no longer appropriate, because no threshold could be identified for the critical effects. It works instead from reference points and compares dietary exposure with them: the lower confidence limit of the benchmark dose at 1% extra risk is 0.50 µg per kg of body weight per day for the neurodevelopmental effects seen in children aged one to seven, 1.5 µg for effects on systolic blood pressure in adults, and 0.63 µg for effects on the kidney. EFSA states that current dietary exposure poses a low to negligible risk for most adults, and that there is potential concern for neurodevelopmental effects in foetuses, infants and children (Scientific Opinion on Lead in Food, EFSA CONTAM Panel, 2010, doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1570).

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC L04AX04).

dose.text: In a monkey study, limb defects appeared in the offspring at every dose tested; this is an animal finding and gives no human dose threshold.
dose.quote: Limb abnormalities were seen in the offspring of monkeys that were dosed with lenalidomide during organogenesis. This effect was seen at all doses tested.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 4.1 Contraindications (Pregnancy), read via openFDA version 41 (DailyMed version 41 published 2026-08-06)

effects.text: In a monkey study, lenalidomide caused limb defects similar to thalidomide's birth defects in humans, and the US label warns it may cause birth defects or embryo-fetal death.
effects.quote: Lenalidomide, a thalidomide analogue, caused limb abnormalities in a developmental monkey study similar to birth defects caused by thalidomide in humans. If lenalidomide is used during pregnancy, it may cause birth defects or embryo-fetal death.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), Boxed Warning, Highlights version (Embryo-fetal toxicity)

before_after.text: A woman who can become pregnant must use effective contraception from at least 4 weeks before lenalidomide to at least 4 weeks after, even during interruptions, unless committed to absolute, continuous, monthly-confirmed abstinence.
before_after.quote: for at least 4 weeks before therapy, during therapy, and until at least 4 weeks after lenalidomide therapy and even in case of dose interruption unless the patient commits to absolute and continuous abstinence confirmed on a monthly basis
before_after.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.4, Contraception (women of childbearing potential) (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

paternal.text: Under the EU product information, men on lenalidomide should use condoms during treatment and dose interruptions and for 1 week after stopping if their partner is pregnant, or could become pregnant without contraception.
paternal.quote: all male patients taking lenalidomide should use condoms throughout treatment duration, during dose interruption and for 1 week after cessation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or of childbearing potential and has no contraception.
paternal.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6, Women of childbearing potential/Contraception in males and females (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

other_effects.text: In animal studies, lenalidomide caused embryo death in pregnant rabbits at 20 times the maximum recommended human dose; this is an animal result.
other_effects.quote: Similar studies in pregnant rabbits and rats at 20 times and 200 times the MRHD respectively, produced embryo lethality in rabbits
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal data, read via openFDA (version 41, effective 2023-03-24)

regulatory.text: The EU product information requires lenalidomide to be prescribed under a Pregnancy Prevention Programme unless there is reliable evidence that the patient does not have childbearing potential.
regulatory.quote: Due to the teratogenic potential, lenalidomide must be prescribed under a Pregnancy Prevention Programme (see section 4.4) unless there is reliable evidence that the patient does not have childbearing potential.
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6 (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

monitoring.text: If a woman becomes pregnant on lenalidomide, treatment must be stopped and she should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with lenalidomide, treatment must be stopped and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6 (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

evidence_base.text: The US label bases its pregnancy warning on lenalidomide's mechanism of action and on animal studies; the label's pregnancy data section presents animal data only.
evidence_base.quote: Based on the mechanism of action [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] and findings from animal studies [see Data] , REVLIMID can cause embryo-fetal harm when administered to a pregnant female
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary, read via openFDA (version 41, effective 2023-03-24)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

regulatory.text: Health Canada's monograph says lithium should not be used in pregnancy or in women who could become pregnant unless no other appropriate therapy can substitute and, in the professional's opinion, benefits outweigh possible hazards.
regulatory.quote: lithium should not be used during pregnancy or in women of child-bearing potential unless it cannot be substituted by other appropriate therapy and in the opinion of the health professional the expected benefits outweigh the possible hazards
regulatory.source_label: Health Canada, CARBOLITH (lithium carbonate) product monograph, section 7.1.1 Pregnant Women (revised 2023-11-22)

window.text: French product information says lithium should not be used in pregnancy, especially in the first 9 weeks counted from the last menstrual period (end of heart formation), unless judged essential for the mother's health.
window.quote: Le traitement au lithium ne doit pas être utilisé pendant la grossesse, en particulier au cours des 9 premières semaines d'aménorrhée (fin de l'organogénèse cardiaque), à moins qu'il ne soit jugé essentiel pour la santé de la mère.
window.source_label: ANSM, TERALITHE 250 mg (lithium carbonate) summary of product characteristics, section 4.6

dose.text: A US Medicaid cohort suggests the link with heart defects is dose-dependent, with a risk about three times that of unexposed infants above 900 mg a day.
dose.quote: Our study also suggests that the association of lithium and cardiac malformations in humans is dose-dependent, with a risk that is increased by a factor of approximately 3 beyond doses of 900 mg per day.
dose.source_label: Patorno et al., N Engl J Med 2017 (US Medicaid cohort, 1,325,563 pregnancies), PMID 28591541, discussion

effects.text: French product information reports a higher overall malformation rate in babies exposed to lithium in the womb, mainly heart defects including Ebstein's anomaly.
effects.quote: Une augmentation du taux global des malformations a été observée chez des enfants exposés in utero au lithium. Les malformations observées sont principalement cardiaques dont la maladie d'Ebstein.
effects.source_label: ANSM, TERALITHE 250 mg (lithium carbonate) summary of product characteristics, section 4.6

other_effects.text: The US label warns that babies exposed late in pregnancy may develop lithium toxicity, including a floppy baby syndrome with neurological, cardiac and liver abnormalities.
other_effects.quote: Lithium toxicity may occur in neonates who were exposed to lithium in late pregnancy. A floppy baby syndrome including neurological, cardiac, and hepatic abnormalities that are similar to those seen with lithium toxicity in adults have been observed.
other_effects.source_label: US prescribing information, lithium carbonate (RemedyRepack, effective 2026-04-27), section 8.1, via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: In a meta-analysis of six cohorts, 7.4% of babies exposed in the first trimester had a major malformation, versus 4.3% in a mood-disorder reference group.
absolute_risk.quote: Lithium exposure during the first trimester was associated with an increased risk of major malformations (pooled prevalence 7·4% [95% CI 4·0-10·7] vs 4·3% [3·7-4·8]; pooled aOR 1·71, 95% CI 1·07-2·72)
absolute_risk.source_label: Munk-Olsen et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2018 (international collaborative meta-analysis of six cohort studies), PMID 29929874

before_after.text: For women of childbearing age, French product information says that when lithium is started, prescribers should exclude pregnancy, put effective contraception in place, inform the woman of the teratogenic risk, and check regularly for pregnancy.
before_after.quote: Chez la femme en âge de procréer, à l'instauration du traitement, on s'assurera de l'absence de grossesse, de la mise en place d'une contraception efficace et la patiente devra être informée du potentiel tératogène du lithium. L'absence de grossesse sera vérifiée régulièrement.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, TERALITHE 250 mg (lithium carbonate) summary of product characteristics, section 4.6

paternal.text: French product information says in-vitro studies and reports in treated men suggest an effect on sperm quality and possible effects on fertility; it gives no advice about pregnancies fathered during treatment.
paternal.quote: Des études in vitro et des cas rapportés chez l'homme traité par le lithium suggèrent un effet sur la qualité du sperme. Le lithium pourrait aussi avoir un impact sur la fertilité humaine.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, TERALITHE 250 mg (lithium carbonate) summary of product characteristics, section 4.6

monitoring.text: The US label advises considering fetal echocardiography between 16 and 20 weeks of gestation when the mother took lithium in the first trimester.
monitoring.quote: Consider fetal echocardiography between 16 and 20 weeks gestation in a woman with first trimester lithium exposure because of the potential increased risk of cardiac malformations.
monitoring.source_label: US prescribing information, lithium carbonate (RemedyRepack, effective 2026-04-27), section 8.1, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: A 2018 meta-analysis of six international cohorts included 727 lithium-exposed pregnancies among 22,124 eligible pregnancies, 557 of them from register-based cohorts.
evidence_base.quote: 22 124 eligible pregnancies were identified across the six cohorts, of which 727 pregnancies were eligible for inclusion in the lithium-exposed group (557 [77%] from register-based cohorts and 170 [23%] from clinical cohorts)
evidence_base.source_label: Munk-Olsen et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2018 (international collaborative meta-analysis of six cohort studies), PMID 29929874

regulatory.text: French ANSM minocycline product information contraindicates cyclines from the second trimester and, as a precaution, prefers that they not be used in the first trimester.
regulatory.quote: par mesure de précaution, il est préférable de ne pas utiliser les cyclines pendant le premier trimestre de la grossesse. A partir du deuxième trimestre de la grossesse, l'administration de cyclines est contre-indiquée.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, MYNOCINE 100 mg gélule (minocycline), RCP section 4.6

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC H03BB02).

window.text: The US label states methimazole can cause fetal harm when given in the first trimester; it counts by trimester and gives no week range.
window.quote: Methimazole crosses the placental membranes and can cause fetal harm when administered in the first trimester of pregnancy.
window.source_label: US FDA label, methimazole tablets, WARNINGS (First Trimester Use of Methimazole and Congenital Malformations), via openFDA

dose.text: In a Korean nationwide cohort, a first-trimester cumulative methimazole dose above 495 mg was associated with higher malformation risk than a low cumulative dose of 1 to 126 mg.
dose.quote: In the MMI group, a high cumulative dose (>495 mg) during the first trimester was associated with an increased risk for malformations compared with a low dose (1 to 126 mg)
dose.source_label: Seo GH, Kim TH, Chung JH. Antithyroid drugs and congenital malformations: a nationwide Korean cohort study. Ann Intern Med 2018;168(6):405-413 (abstract)

effects.text: EU product information for thiamazole (methimazole) reports malformations including a missing patch of skin (aplasia cutis), choanal atresia, facial dysmorphism, exomphalos, oesophageal atresia, omphalomesenteric duct anomaly and ventricular septal defect, naming no limb defects.
effects.quote: Reported malformations include aplasia cutis congenita, craniofacial malformations (choanal atresia; facial dysmorphism), exomphalos, oesophageal atresia, omphalo-mesenteric duct anomaly, and ventricular septal defect.
effects.source_label: EMA PRAC, New product information wording, thiamazole (synonym: methimazole) SmPC 4.6 (EPITT 19238)

absolute_risk.text: In a Danish nationwide register, 9.6% of children exposed to methimazole or carbimazole in early pregnancy had a birth defect diagnosed before age 2, versus 6.7% of unexposed children.
absolute_risk.quote: The overall frequency of birth defects was 6.7% (95% CI, 6.7% to 6.8%) in nonexposed children and higher after exposure to methimazole/carbimazole (9.6%; 95% CI, 8.2% to 11.2%)
absolute_risk.source_label: Andersen SL et al. Maternal thyroid function, use of antithyroid drugs in early pregnancy, and birth defects. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2019;104(12):6040-6048 (abstract)

before_after.text: Canada's methimazole monograph says women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during methimazole therapy, and it gives no period after stopping and no pregnancy test.
before_after.quote: Women of childbearing potential should use effective methods of contraception during methimazole therapy.
before_after.source_label: Health Canada, TAPAZOLE (methimazole tablets) Product Monograph, section 7.1.1 Pregnant Women, revised 19 December 2025

other_effects.text: Canada's monograph says methimazole readily crosses the placenta and can induce goitre and hypothyroidism in the developing fetus.
other_effects.quote: Methimazole readily crosses the placental membranes and can induce goiter and hypothyroidism in the developing fetus.
other_effects.source_label: Health Canada, TAPAZOLE (methimazole tablets) Product Monograph, section 7.1.1 Pregnant Women, revised 19 December 2025

regulatory.text: French product information for thiamazole (Thyrozol) contraindicates treatment combining thiamazole with thyroid hormones during pregnancy, and its contraindications section lists no other pregnancy contraindication.
regulatory.quote: Un traitement associant le thiamazole et des hormones thyroïdiennes est contre-indiqué pendant la grossesse (voir rubrique 4.6).
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, base de données publique des médicaments, THYROZOL 10 mg (thiamazole) RCP section 4.3, page updated 11/04/2023

monitoring.text: Canada's monograph recommends close maternal, fetal and neonatal monitoring when methimazole is used in pregnancy, with the methimazole dose adjusted as necessary.
monitoring.quote: Close maternal, fetal, and neonatal monitoring is recommended, with adjustment of methimazole as necessary.
monitoring.source_label: Health Canada, TAPAZOLE (methimazole tablets) Product Monograph, section 7.1.1 Pregnant Women, revised 19 December 2025

evidence_base.text: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 cohort studies counted 5,957 pregnancy exposures to carbimazole or methimazole, analysed together rather than drug by drug.
evidence_base.quote: We identified 16 cohort studies comprising 5957, 15,785, and 15,666 exposures to CMZ/MMI, PTU, and untreated hyperthyroidism, respectively.
evidence_base.source_label: Agrawal M et al. Antithyroid drug therapy in pregnancy and risk of congenital anomalies: systematic review and meta-analysis. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf) 2022;96(6):857-868 (abstract)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC L01BA01, L04AX03).

window.text: The US label states that methotrexate exposure in the first trimester, counted by trimester of pregnancy, is associated with more miscarriages and multiple developmental problems.
window.quote: Methotrexate exposure during the first trimester of pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of spontaneous abortions and multiple adverse developmental outcomes
window.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

dose.text: The EMA says data are insufficient for exposure in pregnancy above 30 mg a week, but higher rates of miscarriage and malformations are expected, particularly at doses used to treat cancer.
dose.quote: Insufficient data is available for methotrexate exposure during pregnancy higher than 30 mg (15 ml)/week, but higher rates of spontaneous abortions and congenital malformations are expected, in particular at doses commonly used in oncologic indications
dose.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6

effects.text: First-trimester exposure is associated with skull, facial, central nervous system and limb abnormalities (limb defects flagged), and sometimes heart defects and intellectual impairment.
effects.quote: multiple adverse developmental outcomes, including skull anomalies, facial dysmorphism, central nervous system abnormalities, limb abnormalities, and sometimes cardiac anomalies and intellectual impairment
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

absolute_risk.text: Major birth defects occurred in 6.6% of babies born alive after low-dose methotrexate in pregnancy, compared with about 4% of babies born alive to women with the same diseases on other medicines.
absolute_risk.quote: Major birth defects occurred in 6.6% of live births in women exposed to low-dose methotrexate treatment (less than 30 mg [15 ml]/week) during pregnancy, compared to approximately 4% of live births in disease-matched patients
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6

before_after.text: The EU product information requires pregnancy to be excluded before use in non-cancer indications, and effective contraception in women of childbearing potential during treatment and for at least six months after.
before_after.quote: In non-oncologic indications, the absence of pregnancy must be confirmed before Jylamvo is used. If women of child bearing potential are treated, effective contraception must be used during treatment and for at least six months after.
before_after.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.4 (Teratogenicity – Reproductive risk)

paternal.text: As a precaution, the EU product information recommends reliable contraception for sexually active treated men or their female partners until at least 3 months after stopping, and no semen donation until 3 months after.
paternal.quote: recommended to use reliable contraception during treatment of the male patient and for at least 3 months after cessation of methotrexate. Men should not donate semen during therapy or for 3 months following discontinuation of methotrexate.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 (Contraception in males)

other_effects.text: The US label states that exposure in the second and third trimesters is associated with intrauterine growth restriction and functional abnormalities.
other_effects.quote: Adverse outcomes associated with exposure during second and third trimesters of pregnancy include intrauterine growth restriction and functional abnormalities.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

regulatory.text: The US label carries a boxed warning that methotrexate tablets can cause embryo-fetal toxicity, including fetal death, and contraindicates them in pregnancy for non-cancer diseases.
regulatory.quote: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY, HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, SEVERE ADVERSE REACTIONS, AND RISK OF MEDICATION ERRORS Methotrexate tablets can cause embryo-fetal toxicity, including fetal death. For non-neoplastic diseases, methotrexate tablets are contraindicated in pregnancy.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, Boxed Warning (read via openFDA)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs during treatment or up to six months after, the EU product information says to give medical advice on the risk to the child and to perform ultrasound examinations.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs during treatment with methotrexate and up to six months thereafter, medical advice should be given regarding the risk of harmful effects on the child associated with treatment and ultrasonography examinations should be performed
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 (Pregnancy)

evidence_base.text: A prospective multicentre cohort study included 324 pregnancies exposed to methotrexate at 30 mg/week or less, 188 after conception and 136 in the 12 weeks before, plus 459 disease-matched and 1,107 non-autoimmune comparison women.
evidence_base.quote: The study sample included 324 MTX-exposed pregnancies (188 exposed post-conception, 136 exposed pre-conception), 459 disease-matched comparison women, and 1,107 comparison women without autoimmune diseases.
evidence_base.source_label: Weber-Schoendorfer C et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2014;66(5):1101-10, prospective multicenter cohort (PubMed abstract)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC G03BA02, G03EK01).

regulatory.text: The US testosterone enanthate label, like the other US androgen labels read, contraindicates androgens in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.quote: Androgens are contraindicated in men with carcinomas of the breast or with known or suspected carcinomas of the prostate and in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

window.text: The US label, counting by trimester, says masculinisation of a female fetus is most likely when androgens are given in the first trimester, and its degree is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus.
window.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus and is most likely to occur in the female fetus when the drugs are given in the first trimester.
window.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

dose.text: The US methyltestosterone label says the degree of masculinisation is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus, and it states no threshold dose.
dose.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and age of the fetus
dose.source_label: US label, Methitest (methyltestosterone) tablets, Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, Contraindications, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says androgens given in pregnancy virilise the external genitals of a female fetus, with clitoral enlargement, abnormal vaginal development and genital folds fused into a scrotum-like structure.
effects.quote: When administered to pregnant women, androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus. This virilization includes clitoromegaly, abnormal vaginal development, and fusion of genital folds to form a scrotal-like structure.
effects.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

other_effects.text: In animal studies, the US Xyosted label says testosterone exposure in the womb caused hormonal and behavioural changes in offspring as well as structural impairments of reproductive tissues in both sexes.
other_effects.quote: In animal developmental studies, exposure to testosterone in utero resulted in hormonal and behavioral changes in offspring and structural impairments of reproductive tissues in female and male offspring.
other_effects.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

paternal.text: France's ANSM says pregnant women must avoid all contact with testosterone gel application sites, and a man whose partner is pregnant must be especially careful with the precautions against transfer.
paternal.quote: Les femmes enceintes doivent éviter tout contact avec les sites d'application de ce médicament. En cas de grossesse chez sa partenaire, le patient devra être d'autant plus vigilant quant aux précautions d'utilisation
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Androgel 50 mg gel transdermique en sachet-dose, RCP section 4.4 (Transfert peau à peau)

monitoring.text: The US label says a patient who becomes pregnant while taking androgens should be told of the potential hazard to the fetus, and it names no specific prenatal test or newborn check.
monitoring.quote: If the patient becomes pregnant while taking androgens, she should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The Xyosted label bases the statement that testosterone is teratogenic on animal data and its mechanism of action, and it gives no count of exposed human pregnancies.
evidence_base.quote: Testosterone is teratogenic and may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman based on data from animal studies and its mechanism of action
evidence_base.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA
