regulatory.text: French ANSM minocycline product information contraindicates cyclines from the second trimester and, as a precaution, prefers that they not be used in the first trimester.
regulatory.quote: par mesure de précaution, il est préférable de ne pas utiliser les cyclines pendant le premier trimestre de la grossesse. A partir du deuxième trimestre de la grossesse, l'administration de cyclines est contre-indiquée.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, MYNOCINE 100 mg gélule (minocycline), RCP section 4.6

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC A02BB01, G02AD06).

window.text: ANSM says a threefold higher risk of malformations has been reported after first-trimester exposure, and that a low dose used to induce labour at term carries no malformation risk.
window.quote: un risque de malformations fœtales multiplié par trois (incluant le syndrome de Moebius, la maladie des brides amniotiques et des anomalies du système nerveux central) a été rapporté lors de grossesses exposées au misoprostol au cours du premier trimestre.
window.source_label: ANSM, Angusta 25 microgrammes (misoprostol) RCP section 4.6, updated 09/08/2024

effects.text: The US label cites literature reports linking first-trimester misoprostol with skull defects, cranial nerve palsies, facial malformations and limb defects, and warns it can cause abortion and premature birth.
effects.quote: Several reports in the literature associate the use of misoprostol during the first trimester of pregnancy with skull defects, cranial nerve palsies, facial malformations, and limb defects.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cytotec (Pfizer), Pregnancy: Teratogenic effects, and boxed warning

absolute_risk.text: ANSM says pregnancies that continued after a failed abortion with mifepristone and misoprostol, or misoprostol alone, were associated with a threefold higher malformation risk, against about 2 in 100 in controls.
absolute_risk.quote: a été associé à une augmentation par 3 du risque de malformations congénitales dans le cas de grossesses évolutives exposées à la mifépristone et au misoprostol ou au misoprostol seul, comparé au groupe contrôle (environ 2%)
absolute_risk.source_label: ANSM, Gymiso 200 microgrammes (misoprostol) RCP section 4.6, updated 23/12/2025

before_after.text: For NSAID-ulcer prevention, the US label requires a negative serum pregnancy test within 2 weeks before starting and effective contraception, and advises avoiding pregnancy for at least one month or one cycle after stopping.
before_after.quote: It is also important to avoid pregnancy while taking this medication and for at least one month or through one menstrual cycle after you stop taking it.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Cytotec (Pfizer), boxed warning and Patient Information leaflet

other_effects.text: Beyond birth defects, the US label warns misoprostol in pregnancy can cause abortion, premature birth or uterine rupture, and, in obstetric use, fetal bradycardia and fetal death have been reported.
other_effects.quote: CYTOTEC (MISOPROSTOL) ADMINISTRATION TO WOMEN WHO ARE PREGNANT CAN CAUSE BIRTH DEFECTS, ABORTION, PREMATURE BIRTH OR UTERINE RUPTURE.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cytotec (Pfizer), boxed warning and Labor and delivery

regulatory.text: The US label carries a boxed warning, contraindicates use by pregnant women to prevent NSAID ulcers, and allows use in women of childbearing potential only at high ulcer risk and under set conditions.
regulatory.quote: Cytotec should not be taken by pregnant women to reduce the risk of ulcers induced by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Cytotec (Pfizer), boxed warning and Contraindications

monitoring.text: ANSM says that if a woman continues the pregnancy after a failed abortion, a specialised centre should follow it with prenatal ultrasound paying particular attention to the limbs and head.
monitoring.quote: Si la patiente désire poursuivre sa grossesse, un suivi attentif de la grossesse avec échographie prénatale portant une attention particulière aux membres et à la tête, doit être mise en place dans un centre spécialisé.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, RCP GYMISO 200 microgrammes comprimé (misoprostol), section 4.6, updated 23/12/2025

evidence_base.text: A 2006 meta-analysis of misoprostol and birth defects pooled four case-control studies with 4,899 cases of congenital anomalies and 5,742 controls.
evidence_base.quote: Four studies involving 4899 cases of congenital anomalies and 5742 controls were included in accordance with the selection criteria.
evidence_base.source_label: da Silva Dal Pizzol T, Knop FP, Mengue SS. Prenatal exposure to misoprostol and congenital anomalies: systematic review and meta-analysis. Reprod Toxicol 2006;22(4):666-71

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

window.text: The US label says use during pregnancy is associated with higher risks of first-trimester pregnancy loss and of malformations, and it names no narrower window for the malformations.
window.quote: Use during pregnancy is associated with increased risks of first trimester pregnancy loss and congenital malformations.
window.source_label: US FDA label, CellCept (Genentech), Boxed Warning (Embryofetal toxicity), read via openFDA, version 51, effective 2026-08-05

dose.text: In rats and rabbits, mycophenolate caused malformations and pregnancy loss at doses below the recommended human clinical dose; this is an animal finding, not a human threshold.
dose.quote: Oral administration of mycophenolate to rats and rabbits during the period of organogenesis produced congenital malformations and pregnancy loss at doses less than the recommended clinical dose
dose.source_label: US FDA label, CellCept (Genentech), section 8.1 Pregnancy, read via openFDA, version 51 (DailyMed version 51 published 2026-08-10)

effects.text: Documented malformations include anomalies of the distal limbs (a limb defect), defects of the outer ear, eye and face such as cleft lip and palate, and heart, oesophagus, kidney and nervous system defects.
effects.quote: Malformations that have been documented include external ear, eye, and other facial abnormalities including cleft lip and palate, and anomalies of the distal limbs, heart, esophagus, kidney, and nervous system.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, CellCept (Genentech), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data

absolute_risk.text: EMA reports malformations in 23 to 27% of babies exposed during pregnancy, against 4 to 5% in transplant patients on other immunosuppressants and 2 to 3% in the overall population.
absolute_risk.quote: The reported incidence of malformation in the offspring of mothers exposed to mycophenolate during pregnancy is 23 to 27% compared with 4 to 5% in transplant patients treated with other immunosuppressants, and 2 to 3% in the overall population.
absolute_risk.source_label: European Medicines Agency press release, 'EMA recommends additional measures to prevent use of mycophenolate in pregnancy'

before_after.text: Women who can become pregnant must use at least one reliable contraceptive method before starting mycophenolate, during treatment and for six weeks after stopping, unless they choose abstinence.
before_after.quote: women of childbearing potential must use at least one form of reliable contraception (see section 4.3) before starting the therapy, during therapy, and for six weeks after stopping the therapy, unless abstinence is the chosen method of contraception.
before_after.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

paternal.text: As a precaution, a sexually active man taking mycophenolate or his female partner is recommended to use reliable contraception during his treatment and for at least 90 days after he stops.
paternal.quote: Therefore, the following precautionary measures are recommended: sexually active male patients or their female partners are recommended to use reliable contraception during treatment of the male patient and for at least 90 days after cessation of mycophenolate mofetil.
paternal.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6, subsection Men (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

other_effects.text: Beyond malformations, spontaneous abortion has been reported in 45 to 49% of pregnant women exposed to mycophenolate mofetil, against 12 to 33% in solid organ transplant patients on other immunosuppressants.
other_effects.quote: Spontaneous abortions have been reported in 45 to 49% of pregnant women exposed to mycophenolate mofetil, compared to a reported rate of between 12 and 33% in solid organ transplant patients treated with immunosuppressants other than mycophenolate mofetil.
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6, subsection Pregnancy (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

regulatory.text: The EU product information contraindicates mycophenolate in pregnancy unless there is no suitable alternative treatment to prevent transplant rejection.
regulatory.quote: Therefore, treatment is contraindicated in pregnancy unless there are no suitable alternative treatments to prevent transplant rejection.
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.4, subsection Teratogenic effects (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs or is suspected during or shortly after treatment, the patient should not stop taking mycophenolate but must contact their doctor immediately.
monitoring.quote: Advice on action if a pregnancy occurs or is suspected during or shortly after being treated with mycophenolate mofetil. Patients will be informed that they should not stop taking mycophenolate mofetil but must contact their doctor immediately.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), Annex II.D, key elements of the educational materials (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

evidence_base.text: A US transplant registry cohort covered 382 pregnancies in kidney recipients managed on mycophenolate, grouped by when each woman stopped it, some before conception, so not all were exposed in pregnancy.
evidence_base.quote: Data from the National Transplantation Pregnancy Registry included 382 cases in which KTRs managed on MPA became pregnant. Overall, 22 variables, including the time in which a KTR discontinued MPA, were assessed
evidence_base.source_label: King RW et al., Pregnancy Outcomes Related to Mycophenolate Exposure in Female Kidney Transplant Recipients, Am J Transplant 2017;17(1):151-160, abstract (retrospective cohort, US National Transplantation Pregnancy Registry)

dose.text: EMA tobramycin inhalation product information says aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm such as congenital deafness when high systemic concentrations are reached, and systemic exposure after inhalation is very low.

effects.text: US aminoglycoside labeling reports several cases of total irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy.

other_effects.text: French tobramycin product information advises against use in pregnancy because of a potential risk of fetal ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and restricts use to serious infections.

absolute_risk.text: A CDC systematic review reports hearing or vestibular deficits in 18 of 121 children (15%) after prenatal streptomycin exposure, pooled from 2 cohort studies and 2 case series, with no unexposed comparison group given.

absolute_risk.source_label: Yu PA et al. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50 (CDC systematic review)

monitoring.text: French tobramycin product information recommends assessing the newborn's hearing (otoacoustic emissions) and kidney function after exposure during pregnancy.

monitoring.source_label: ANSM, NEBCINE 100 mg solution injectable (tobramycin), RCP section 4.6

evidence_base.text: A CDC systematic review of published studies and case reports counted 9 prenatal exposures to amikacin, 345 to gentamicin, 285 to streptomycin and 43 to tobramycin.

regulatory.text: The US testosterone enanthate label, like the other US androgen labels read, contraindicates androgens in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.quote: Androgens are contraindicated in men with carcinomas of the breast or with known or suspected carcinomas of the prostate and in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

window.text: The US label, counting by trimester, says masculinisation of a female fetus is most likely when androgens are given in the first trimester, and its degree is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus.
window.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus and is most likely to occur in the female fetus when the drugs are given in the first trimester.
window.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

dose.text: The US methyltestosterone label says the degree of masculinisation is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus, and it states no threshold dose.
dose.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and age of the fetus
dose.source_label: US label, Methitest (methyltestosterone) tablets, Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, Contraindications, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says androgens given in pregnancy virilise the external genitals of a female fetus, with clitoral enlargement, abnormal vaginal development and genital folds fused into a scrotum-like structure.
effects.quote: When administered to pregnant women, androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus. This virilization includes clitoromegaly, abnormal vaginal development, and fusion of genital folds to form a scrotal-like structure.
effects.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

other_effects.text: In animal studies, the US Xyosted label says testosterone exposure in the womb caused hormonal and behavioural changes in offspring as well as structural impairments of reproductive tissues in both sexes.
other_effects.quote: In animal developmental studies, exposure to testosterone in utero resulted in hormonal and behavioral changes in offspring and structural impairments of reproductive tissues in female and male offspring.
other_effects.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

paternal.text: France's ANSM says pregnant women must avoid all contact with testosterone gel application sites, and a man whose partner is pregnant must be especially careful with the precautions against transfer.
paternal.quote: Les femmes enceintes doivent éviter tout contact avec les sites d'application de ce médicament. En cas de grossesse chez sa partenaire, le patient devra être d'autant plus vigilant quant aux précautions d'utilisation
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Androgel 50 mg gel transdermique en sachet-dose, RCP section 4.4 (Transfert peau à peau)

monitoring.text: The US label says a patient who becomes pregnant while taking androgens should be told of the potential hazard to the fetus, and it names no specific prenatal test or newborn check.
monitoring.quote: If the patient becomes pregnant while taking androgens, she should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The Xyosted label bases the statement that testosterone is teratogenic on animal data and its mechanism of action, and it gives no count of exposed human pregnancies.
evidence_base.quote: Testosterone is teratogenic and may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman based on data from animal studies and its mechanism of action
evidence_base.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

regulatory.text: French ANSM minocycline product information contraindicates cyclines from the second trimester and, as a precaution, prefers that they not be used in the first trimester.
regulatory.quote: par mesure de précaution, il est préférable de ne pas utiliser les cyclines pendant le premier trimestre de la grossesse. A partir du deuxième trimestre de la grossesse, l'administration de cyclines est contre-indiquée.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, MYNOCINE 100 mg gélule (minocycline), RCP section 4.6

window.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling places the tooth discoloration risk during tooth development, defined as the last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years.
window.quote: The use of drugs of the tetracycline-class during tooth development (last half of pregnancy, infancy and childhood to the age of 8 years) may cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown).
window.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

dose.text: FDA tetracycline-class labeling says tooth discoloration is more common with long-term use but has also been seen after repeated short-term courses.
dose.quote: This adverse reaction is more common during long-term use of the drugs but it has been observed following repeated short-term courses.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tetracycline hydrochloride capsules (Amneal), Warnings: Tooth Development

effects.text: FDA minocycline labeling mentions rare spontaneous postmarketing reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction, and says limited information allows no conclusion on a causal association.
effects.quote: Rare spontaneous reports of congenital anomalies including limb reduction have been reported in postmarketing experience. Only limited information is available regarding these reports; therefore, no conclusion on causal association can be established.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride (Northwind Health), Pregnancy: Risk Summary

other_effects.text: FDA labeling says tetracycline-class drugs, including minocycline, may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when given in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Tetracycline class drugs, including minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets may cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and reversible inhibition of bone growth when administered during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: In a Swedish national cohort, major malformations occurred in 39.75 per 1000 infants exposed to tetracyclines in the first trimester versus 38.76 per 1000 propensity-matched unexposed infants.
absolute_risk.quote: The prevalence of any MCMs among tetracycline-exposed infants was 39.75 cases per 1000 infants (95% CI, 35.14-44.93 cases per 1000 infants; 252 infants) and that among unexposed infants was 38.76 cases per 1000 infants
absolute_risk.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. First Trimester Tetracycline Exposure and Risk of Major Congenital Malformations. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055

monitoring.text: FDA minocycline extended-release labeling says to advise a patient who becomes pregnant during treatment of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.quote: If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, advise the patient of the risk to the fetus and to discontinue treatment.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, minocycline hydrochloride extended-release tablets (PD-Rx), 8.1 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: A Swedish nationwide cohort, described by its authors as substantially larger than previous reports rather than as the largest, included 6340 first-trimester-exposed infants: 4962 exposed to doxycycline, 1199 to lymecycline, 180 to tetracycline and 13 to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.quote: Among the 6340 exposed infants (3325 male [52.4%]), 4962 (78.3%) were exposed to doxycycline, 1199 (18.9%) to lymecycline, 180 (2.8%) to tetracycline, and 13 (0.2%) to oxytetracycline.
evidence_base.source_label: Nakitanda AO et al. JAMA Netw Open 2024;7(11):e2445055 (Swedish nationwide register cohort)

regulatory.text: The US label contraindicates penicillamine in pregnancy, except for the treatment of Wilson's disease or certain patients with cystinuria.
regulatory.quote: Except for the treatment of Wilson's disease or certain patients with cystinuria, use of penicillamine during pregnancy is contraindicated
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Contraindications (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

dose.text: In animal studies, the US label says penicillamine was teratogenic in rats at doses six times higher than the highest recommended human dose.
dose.quote: Penicillamine has been shown to be teratogenic in rats when given in doses six times higher than the highest dose recommended for human use.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says congenital cutis laxa and associated birth defects have been reported in babies exposed during pregnancy, although normal outcomes have also been reported.
effects.quote: Although normal outcomes have been reported, characteristic congenital cutis laxa and associated birth defects have been reported in infants born of mothers who received therapy with penicillamine during pregnancy.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

other_effects.text: The UK label reports several cases of reversible cutis laxa in infants whose mothers with Wilson's disease took penicillamine throughout pregnancy.
other_effects.quote: There have been several cases of reversible cutis laxa in infants born to mothers taking penicillamine throughout pregnancy.
other_effects.source_label: MHRA, Distamine 250 mg film-coated tablets SmPC, section 4.6 (revised 14/07/2026)

absolute_risk.text: Summarising the 2018 Pfeiffenberger cohort, a 2022 systematic review reports malformations in 3.3% of babies of mothers on penicillamine; it gives no numeric comparison rate for that figure.
absolute_risk.quote: Fetal malformations were observed in 3.3% of babies from mothers on DPA, 2.7% on trientine (comparable with the general population) and none on zinc.
absolute_risk.source_label: Litwin et al., Biomedicines 2022, systematic review and meta-analysis of pregnancy in Wilson's disease (PMC9495510), citing Pfeiffenberger et al. 2018

before_after.text: ANSM says treatment for Wilson disease must not be stopped during pregnancy and that, outside such cases, effective contraception is recommended.
before_after.quote: Dans le cas de la maladie de Wilson, le traitement ne doit pas être arrêté pendant la grossesse. En dehors de ces cas, une contraception efficace est recommandée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, Trolovol 300 mg comprimé pelliculé, RCP section 4.6 (updated 25/02/2026)

monitoring.text: The US label says women of childbearing potential on penicillamine should promptly report a missed period and be followed closely for early recognition of pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: Women on therapy with penicillamine who are of childbearing potential should be apprised of this risk, advised to report promptly any missed menstrual periods or other indications of possible pregnancy, and followed closely for early recognition of pregnancy.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The 2022 systematic review rests on 13 retrospective studies and 36 case series or reports, covering 822 pregnancies in 449 women with Wilson disease, not all exposed to penicillamine.
evidence_base.quote: We found 49 publications, including 13 retrospective studies and 36 series and case reports on pregnancy outcomes in WD patients. In total, descriptions of 449 pregnant women with 822 pregnancies were retrieved.
evidence_base.source_label: Litwin et al., Biomedicines 2022, systematic review and meta-analysis of pregnancy in Wilson's disease (PMC9495510)

entries.name: Phenindione

sources.label: ENTIS expert list of known human structural teratogens
sources.note: Phenindione is on the list of medicines that ENTIS experts identify as known human structural teratogens (Bluett-Duncan M et al. A Scoping Review of Human Teratogens and Their Impact on the Developing Brain. Birth Defects Res. 2025;117(9):e2497).

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

window.text: In an ENTIS multicentre cohort of vitamin K antagonist exposures (only 2 with phenindione), coumarin embryopathy risk was very small, especially when first-trimester therapy stopped by week 8, counted from the last menstrual period.
window.quote: The risk for coumarin embryopathy is, however, very small, in particular when therapy during the 1(st) trimester did not take place later than week 8 after the 1(st) day of the last menstrual period.
window.source_label: Schaefer C et al. Vitamin K antagonists and pregnancy outcome. A multi-centre prospective study (ENTIS, 666 exposed vs 1,094 controls). Thromb Haemost 2006;95(6):949-57, PubMed abstract

effects.text: The ENTIS consensus lists, for the anticoagulant group including phenindione, multiple malformations including nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, skeletal and digital (finger or toe) defects, growth disruption and facial dysmorphia.
effects.quote: Multiple malformations including nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, skeletal and digital. Growth disruption. Facial dysmorphia.
effects.source_label: Bluett-Duncan M et al. ENTIS expert consensus, Birth Defects Res 2025;117(9):e2497, Table 1, anticoagulant row (one cell spanning acenocoumarol, phenindione, warfarin)

absolute_risk.text: A meta-analysis in women with mechanical heart valves, counting phenindione among vitamin K antagonists, found anticoagulant-related embryopathy or fetopathy in about 2% of fetuses exposed to them throughout pregnancy at standard INR targets.
absolute_risk.quote: Anticoagulant-related embryopathy and foetopathy was seen in approximately 2% of the foetuses exposed to VKAs throughout pregnancy.
absolute_risk.source_label: D'Souza R et al. Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516, open-access full text, Results and Table 1 (vitamin K antagonists, INR target 2.5-3.5, 12/407)

before_after.text: The UK label says women of child-bearing age treated with phenindione should be cautioned about possible pregnancy complications; it sets no contraception duration, washout period or pregnancy test.
before_after.quote: Women of child-bearing age who are treated with Dindevan should be cautioned about the possible complications of pregnancy.
before_after.source_label: UK Summary of Product Characteristics, Dindevan 25mg Tablets / Phenindione 25mg Tablets (Mercury Pharma Group / ADVANZ Pharma), section 4.6, date of revision 19/02/2024, on emc

other_effects.text: In women with mechanical heart valves, a meta-analysis counting phenindione among vitamin K antagonists found a 1.4% fetopathy risk (central nervous system or eye abnormalities) from second- and third-trimester exposure after first-trimester heparin.
other_effects.quote: Also, although sequential treatment eliminates the risk of anticoagulant-related embryopathy, the risk of anticoagulant-related foetopathy from second- and third-trimester exposure is 1.4%.
other_effects.source_label: D'Souza R et al. Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516, open-access full text, Discussion

regulatory.text: The UK phenindione label contraindicates oral anticoagulant therapy in pregnancy because of possible teratogenicity and the risk of fetal haemorrhage near term.
regulatory.quote: Oral anticoagulant therapy is contraindicated in pregnancy because of possible teratogenicity and the risk of foetal haemorrhage near term.
regulatory.source_label: UK Summary of Product Characteristics, Dindevan 25mg Tablets / Phenindione 25mg Tablets (Mercury Pharma Group / ADVANZ Pharma), sections 4.3 and 4.6, date of revision 19/02/2024, on emc

monitoring.text: An ENTIS multicentre cohort study recommends close obstetric follow-up, including a level II (detailed) ultrasound scan, after any vitamin K antagonist exposure during pregnancy, a class that includes phenindione.
monitoring.quote: Close follow-up by the obstetrician including level II ultrasound should be recommended in any case of VKA exposure during pregnancy.
monitoring.source_label: Schaefer C et al. Vitamin K antagonists and pregnancy outcome. A multi-centre prospective study (ENTIS, 12 centres). Thromb Haemost 2006;95(6):949-57, PubMed abstract

evidence_base.text: An ENTIS multicentre prospective study compared 666 pregnant women exposed to vitamin K antagonists, including 2 exposed to phenindione, with a non-exposed control group of 1,094 women.
evidence_base.quote: we compared 666 pregnant women exposed to phenprocoumon (n = 280), acenocoumarol (n = 226), fluindione (n = 99), warfarin (n = 63) and phenindione (n = 2) to a non-exposed control group (n = 1,094).
evidence_base.source_label: Schaefer C et al. Vitamin K antagonists and pregnancy outcome. A multi-centre prospective study (ENTIS, 12 centres). Thromb Haemost 2006;95(6):949-57, PubMed abstract

entries.name: Phenobarbital

sources.label: ENTIS expert list of known human structural teratogens
sources.note: Phenobarbital is on the list of medicines that ENTIS experts identify as known human structural teratogens (Bluett-Duncan M et al. A Scoping Review of Human Teratogens and Their Impact on the Developing Brain. Birth Defects Res. 2025;117(9):e2497).

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

window.text: The North American registry measured the malformation risk in babies whose mothers took phenobarbital during the first trimester of pregnancy (counting basis: trimester).
window.quote: The risk of major malformations was estimated among infants exposed to specific ASMs in monotherapy during the first trimester of pregnancy.
window.source_label: Hernandez-Diaz et al. (North American AED Pregnancy Registry), Neurology 2025;105(3):e213786

dose.text: The UK regulator concluded that the higher malformation risk with phenobarbital is dose-dependent but that no dose has been found to be without risk.
dose.quote: the increased risk seen with carbamazepine, phenobarbital and topiramate is dose-dependent but no dose has been found to be without risk
dose.source_label: MHRA UK Public Assessment Report, Antiepileptic drugs: review of safety of use during pregnancy (Key conclusions)

effects.text: Phenobarbital alone is associated with a higher risk of cleft lip and palate and heart defects, and hypospadias, facial dysmorphism, neural tube effects, microcephaly and finger malformations (limb/digit flag) have also been reported.
effects.quote: les fentes labiales et palatines et les malformations cardiovasculaires. D'autres malformations impliquant divers systèmes de l’organisme, notamment des cas d'hypospadias, des caractéristiques faciales dysmorphiques, des effets sur le tube neural, une dysmorphie crâniofaciale (microcéphalie) et des malformations des doigts
effects.source_label: ANSM, RCP GARDENAL 100 mg comprimé (phénobarbital), section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: The UK regulator states that most studies support malformations in 5 to 6 in 100 children exposed to phenobarbital alone, against 2 to 3 in 100 in the general population.
absolute_risk.quote: most individual studies support that 5-6% of children exposed to phenobarbital monotherapy during pregnancy suffer from congenital malformations. This risk is increased compared with children of mothers who were not exposed to antiepileptics during pregnancy (2-3% in general population)
absolute_risk.source_label: MHRA UK Public Assessment Report, Antiepileptic drugs: review of safety of use during pregnancy (Key findings for phenobarbital)

before_after.text: The French label says women of childbearing potential must use effective contraception during phenobarbital treatment and for 2 months after the last dose, and a pregnancy test should be considered before starting.
before_after.quote: Les femmes en âge de procréer doivent utiliser une contraception efficace pendant le traitement et pendant 2 mois après la dernière prise.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP GARDENAL 100 mg comprimé (phénobarbital), sections 4.4 and 4.6

other_effects.text: The UK regulator concluded that, although human studies are inconsistent, the data taken with animal (non-clinical) studies support possible adverse effects of phenobarbital on the child's neurodevelopment.
other_effects.quote: for phenobarbital and phenytoin, although the clinical studies report inconsistent findings, considering these alongside the non-clinical studies which demonstrate a possible effect, the totality of the data support the possibility of adverse effects on neurodevelopment
other_effects.source_label: MHRA UK Public Assessment Report, Antiepileptic drugs: review of safety of use during pregnancy (Key conclusions)

regulatory.text: The French label says phenobarbital must not be used in women of childbearing potential unless the potential benefit is judged to outweigh the risks after other suitable treatment options are assessed.
regulatory.quote: Le phénobarbital ne doit pas être utilisé chez les femmes en âge de procréer à moins que le bénéfice potentiel ne soit jugé supérieur aux risques après évaluation des autres options thérapeutiques appropriées.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, RCP GARDENAL 100 mg comprimé (phénobarbital), section 4.4

monitoring.text: When phenobarbital is used in pregnancy, the French label requires specialised prenatal monitoring aimed at the malformations it describes, such as clefts and heart defects.
monitoring.quote: Une surveillance prénatale spécialisée orientée sur les malformations décrites ci-dessus doit être instaurée.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, RCP GARDENAL 100 mg comprimé (phénobarbital), section 4.6

evidence_base.text: On congenital malformations, the UK regulator's review drew on three meta-analyses and other epidemiological studies involving around 1,800 phenobarbital-exposed pregnancies, including 600 exposed in the first trimester.
evidence_base.quote: These clinical studies, involving around 1800 pregnancies exposed to phenobarbital (including 600 pregnancies exposed in the first trimester), show an increased risk of major congenital malformations following phenobarbital exposure
evidence_base.source_label: MHRA UK Public Assessment Report, Antiepileptic drugs: review of safety of use during pregnancy (section 3.6 Phenobarbital, Congenital malformations)

Coumarin embryopathy after intrauterine exposure to vitamin K antagonists within the first 10 postmenstrual weeks
Successful pregnancy in pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic lupus erythematosus: a case report

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC B01AA04).

regulatory.text: Austria's Marcoumar label contraindicates phenprocoumon in pregnancy, with one exception: an absolute need for anticoagulation when heparin intolerance is life-threatening.
regulatory.quote: Schwangerschaft; Ausnahme: absolute Indikation zur Antikoagulation bei lebensbedrohlicher Heparin-Unverträglichkeit (siehe Abschnitt 4.6).
regulatory.source_label: Austrian BASG Fachinformation (SmPC), Marcoumar Tabletten (phenprocoumon 3 mg), Z.Nr. 8096, Stand der Information 06.2026, section 4.3 Gegenanzeigen

window.text: The Swiss label states that the rate of serious birth defects is strongly raised when phenprocoumon treatment continues beyond the fifth week of gestation.
window.quote: le taux de malformations congénitales graves est fortement élevé lorsque le traitement par phenprocoumone est poursuivi au-delà de la cinquième semaine de gestation
window.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

dose.text: A systematic review of women with mechanical heart valves cites registry data that did not show less fetal loss with low first-trimester VKA doses, defined for phenprocoumon as 3 mg per day or less.
dose.quote: recent data from the Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac disease (ROPAC) registry did not demonstrate reduced foetal loss with the use of low first-trimester doses of VKAs [warfarin ≤5 mg/day, acenocoumarol ≤2 mg/day or phenprocoumon ≤3 mg/day)]
dose.source_label: D'Souza R et al. Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516 (PMC5429939), Discussion

effects.text: Citing warfarin, the Swiss label reports chondrodysplasia (Conradi-Hünermann) after first-trimester exposure and growth disorders with microcephaly and optic atrophy after second- and third-trimester exposure.
effects.quote: Lors d'exposition à la warfarine, des chondrodysplasies (maladie de Conradi-Hünermann) ont été observées au cours du 1er trimestre de gestation, ainsi que des troubles de la croissance avec microencéphalie et atrophie du nerf optique aux 2e et 3e trimestres.
effects.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Données précliniques, Toxicité sur la reproduction

other_effects.text: The Swiss label warns that exposure in the second and third trimesters raises the fetal risk of intrauterine or birth-related (cerebral) bleeding from fetal anticoagulation.
other_effects.quote: Dans les cas d'exposition au phenprocoumone au cours des deuxième et troisième trimestres de grossesse, il existe, pour le fœtus, un risque accru d'hémorragie (cérébrale) intra-utérine ou parturitionnelle résultant de l'anticoagulation fœtale.
other_effects.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

absolute_risk.text: In a cohort of 408 first-trimester phenprocoumon pregnancies, major birth defects occurred in 7.4% versus 2.3% of comparison pregnancies not exposed to VKA or other major teratogens (adjusted odds ratio 2.14).
absolute_risk.quote: the overall rate of major birth defects was significantly increased (7.4 % vs 2.3 %; adjusted odds ratio [ORadj] 2.14; 95 % confidence interval [CI] 1.4-3.4)

before_after.text: The Swiss label states that women of childbearing age taking phenprocoumon must use effective contraception during treatment and for three months after the last dose.
before_after.quote: Les femmes en âge de procréer qui prennent Marcoumar doivent utiliser des mesures contraceptives efficaces au cours du traitement et pendant les trois mois suivant la dernière dose.
before_after.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs on phenprocoumon, the Swiss label advises an immediate switch to a safer treatment such as heparin and close pregnancy follow-up including level II ultrasound.
monitoring.quote: Si une grossesse survient chez une patiente prenant Marcoumar, il convient d'instaurer immédiatement un traitement alternatif plus sûr (p.ex. héparine) et de suivre la grossesse de près, y compris au moyen d'échographies de niveau II.
monitoring.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

evidence_base.text: The largest phenprocoumon-specific study read is an observational cohort comparing 408 exposed pregnancies with 1,642 pregnancies unexposed to VKA or other major teratogens.
evidence_base.quote: Four hundred eight pregnancies with phenprocoumon exposure were compared to 1,642 pregnancies neither exposed to VKA nor to other major teratogens or fetotoxicants.
evidence_base.source_label: Hüttel E et al. Pregnancy outcome of first trimester exposure to the vitamin K antagonist phenprocoumon depends on duration of treatment. Thromb Haemost 2017;117(5):870-879 (PMID 28229160), abstract

sources.label: ENTIS expert list of known human structural teratogens
sources.note: Primidone is on the list of medicines that ENTIS experts identify as known human structural teratogens (Bluett-Duncan M et al. A Scoping Review of Human Teratogens and Their Impact on the Developing Brain. Birth Defects Res. 2025;117(9):e2497).

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it.

window.text: The French product information says use in the third trimester may cause withdrawal symptoms in the newborn, such as sedation, low muscle tone and poor sucking (counting basis: trimester).
window.quote: En cas d'utilisation au cours du troisième trimestre de la grossesse, des symptômes de sevrage peuvent survenir chez le nouveau-né, notamment une sédation, une hypotonie et un trouble de la succion.
window.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 4.6

dose.text: Under a heading on the risks of primidone and of phenobarbital, its main metabolite, the French label says the malformation risk is dose-dependent and that no dose has proved risk-free.
dose.quote: Le risque est dose-dépendant ; cependant, aucune dose ne s'est avérée dépourvue de risque.
dose.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 4.6

effects.text: The French primidone label says phenobarbital alone is associated with cleft lip and palate and heart defects, with hypospadias, neural tube effects, microcephaly and digit anomalies (limb/digit flag) also reported.
effects.quote: de fentes labiales et palatines, et de malformations cardiovasculaires. D'autres malformations impliquant divers systèmes corporels ont également été signalées : notamment des cas d'hypospadias, de dysmorphies faciales, d'effets sur le tube neural, de dysmorphies cranio-faciales (microcéphalie) et d'anomalies digitales.
effects.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: A Cochrane review found malformations in 7.9% of primidone-exposed children in pooled cohort data (95% CI 2.6% to 21.5%), but calls this evidence, from 112 pregnancies, extremely limited and urges caution.
absolute_risk.quote: Evidence pertaining to PRM was extremely limited to 112 pregnancies and caution is warranted when interpreting results. Pooled data from included cohort studies gave a malformation prevalence of 7.9% (95% CI 2.6 to 21.5%).
absolute_risk.source_label: Bromley et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023;8:CD010224 (Monotherapy treatment of epilepsy in pregnancy), Discussion

before_after.text: The French label says women of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception during primidone treatment and for 2 months after the last dose, and a pregnancy test should be considered before starting.
before_after.quote: Les femmes en âge de procréer doivent utiliser une méthode contraceptive hautement efficace pendant le traitement et pendant 2 mois après la dernière prise.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), sections 4.4 and 4.6

paternal.text: The French patient leaflet tells men and women of childbearing age to use effective contraception during treatment and until 2 months after stopping, although the prescriber's summary addresses contraception for women only.
paternal.quote: Si vous êtes un homme ou une femme en âge d’avoir des enfants, sous devez utiliser une contraception efficace pendant et jusqu’à 2 mois après l’arrêt du traitement.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Notice MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 2, Avertissements et précautions

other_effects.text: The French primidone label says studies of neurodevelopmental disorders in children exposed in pregnancy to phenobarbital, primidone's main metabolite, are contradictory and a risk cannot be excluded.
other_effects.quote: Les études relatives au risque de troubles du développement neurologique chez les enfants exposés au phénobarbital pendant la grossesse sont contradictoires, et un risque ne peut être exclu.
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 4.6

regulatory.text: The French label says primidone must not be used in women of childbearing potential or pregnant women unless the potential benefit is judged to outweigh the risks after other suitable options are assessed.
regulatory.quote: La primidone ne doit pas être utilisée chez les femmes en âge de procréer et les femmes enceintes, sauf si le bénéfice potentiel est jugé supérieur aux risques, après évaluation des autres options thérapeutiques appropriées.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, RCP MYSOLINE 250 mg comprimé sécable (primidone), section 4.4

monitoring.text: The US Mysoline label says pregnant women on anticonvulsant therapy, including primidone, should receive prophylactic vitamin K1 for 1 month before, and during, delivery.
monitoring.quote: Pregnant women under anticonvulsant therapy should receive prophylactic vitamin K1 therapy for 1 month prior to, and during, delivery.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, MYSOLINE (primidone) tablets, NDA009170, Warnings: Pregnancy (openFDA, effective 2026-09-10)

evidence_base.text: A Cochrane systematic review found data on only 112 primidone-exposed children, from seven cohort studies, with 7.9% major malformations (95% CI 2.6% to 21.5%).
evidence_base.quote: The prevalence of major malformations (any type) in cohort studies for children exposed to primidone (PRM) (N = 112), based on data from seven studies, was 7.9% (95% CI 2.6 to 21.5)
evidence_base.source_label: Bromley et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023;8:CD010224 (Monotherapy treatment of epilepsy in pregnancy), Results: Primidone

regulatory.text: Propylthiouracil may be the treatment of choice when an antithyroid drug is indicated during or just prior to the first trimester of pregnancy, per the US boxed warning on liver injury.
regulatory.quote: Propylthiouracil may be the treatment of choice when an antithyroid drug is indicated during or just prior to the first trimester of pregnancy
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, propylthiouracil tablets (Macleods), via openFDA

window.text: The sensitive window for malformations is gestational week 6 to 10 counted from the last menstrual period, equivalent to embryonic week 4 to 8 from conception.
window.quote: During gestational week 6–10 (embryonic week 4–8), tissues and organs rapidly develop, and it is the period that is most sensitive to teratogenic exposures and abnormal development.
window.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Severity of birth defects after propylthiouracil exposure in early pregnancy, Thyroid 2014 (Danish nationwide registry cohort)

dose.text: A meta-analysis notes that the only study reporting a dose-response found larger malformation risks with high cumulative methimazole or carbimazole doses, but not with PTU.
dose.quote: This was also the only study to report a dose–response relationship and observed larger risk estimates for congenital anomalies with high cumulative doses of CBZ/MMI but not with PTU.
dose.source_label: Morales DR et al., Antithyroid drug use during pregnancy and the risk of birth defects: systematic review and meta-analysis, Br J Clin Pharmacol 2021

effects.text: Danish registry cases after early-pregnancy PTU were face and neck defects (preauricular and branchial sinus, fistula or cyst) and urinary defects (single kidney cyst, hydronephrosis).
effects.quote: 7 children were diagnosed with a birth defect in the face and neck region (preauricular and branchial sinus/fistula/cyst) and 7 children had a birth defect in the urinary system (single cyst of kidney and hydronephrosis)
effects.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Severity of birth defects after propylthiouracil exposure in early pregnancy, Thyroid 2014 (Danish nationwide registry cohort)

other_effects.text: PTU crosses the placenta and can cause fetal goiter and cretinism (congenital hypothyroidism) when given to a pregnant woman.
other_effects.quote: Propylthiouracil crosses the placenta and can cause fetal goiter and cretinism when administered to a pregnant woman
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, propylthiouracil tablets (Macleods), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: In a Danish nationwide cohort, birth defects diagnosed before age 2 affected 8.3% of children exposed to PTU in early pregnancy, against 6.7% of nonexposed children.
absolute_risk.quote: The overall frequency of birth defects was 6.7% (95% CI, 6.7% to 6.8%) in nonexposed children and higher after exposure to methimazole/carbimazole (9.6%; 95% CI, 8.2% to 11.2%) and propylthiouracil (8.3%; 95% CI, 6.7% to 10.3%).
absolute_risk.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Maternal thyroid function, use of antithyroid drugs in early pregnancy, and birth defects, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2019 (Danish nationwide cohort)

before_after.text: Health Canada suggests PTU before conception and in the first trimester where clinically appropriate, because methimazole carries a higher risk of congenital abnormalities during first-trimester organogenesis.
before_after.quote: is suggested for use prior to conception and in the first trimester of pregnancy where clinically appropriate due to the higher risk of congenital abnormalities with methimazole during fetal organogenesis in the first trimester
before_after.source_label: Health Canada product monograph, Propylthiouracil Tablets (Phebra Canada)

monitoring.text: In 2019 the EMA's PRAC asked that EU product information state that close maternal, foetal and neonatal monitoring is recommended whenever propylthiouracil is used during pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: If propylthiouracil is used during pregnancy, close maternal, foetal and neonatal monitoring is recommended.
monitoring.source_label: EMA PRAC recommendations on signals, propylthiouracil and risk of congenital anomalies (EPITT 19358), EMA/PRAC/303951/2019

evidence_base.text: A 2022 meta-analysis pooled 16 cohort studies including 15,785 PTU exposures and found an adjusted risk ratio of 1.16 for congenital anomalies against nondisease controls.
evidence_base.quote: We identified 16 cohort studies comprising 5957, 15,785, and 15,666 exposures to CMZ/MMI, PTU, and untreated hyperthyroidism, respectively.
evidence_base.source_label: Agrawal M et al., Antithyroid drug therapy in pregnancy and risk of congenital anomalies: systematic review and meta-analysis, Clin Endocrinol 2022

exposure.why: Retinol and its esters condition the skin in creams and lotions; the EU caps them and requires the label 'Consider your daily intake before use'.
exposure.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/996, Annex III entry 376
exposure.basis: The EU's scientific committee counts harm to the unborn child among vitamin A's critical effects and limits it in cosmetics so that total intake stays within safe limits; no authority rates skin use itself.

entries.exposure_why: High-dose vitamin A comes from supplements or treatment; California lists it only above 10,000 IU a day.

limit.text: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III caps Retinol, Retinyl Acetate and Retinyl Palmitate at 0.05% Retinol Equivalent in body lotion and 0.3% RE in other leave-on and rinse-off products, under Regulation (EU) 2024/996.
limit.quote: For any cosmetic product containing Retinol, Retinyl Acetate or Retinyl Palmitate the following, labelling is obligatory: 'Contains Vitamin A. Consider your daily intake before use'.

effects.text: SCCS cites a prospective study in which mothers taking over 4500 mg retinol equivalent daily had a 3.5-fold higher risk of a child born with cranial-neural-crest defects.
effects.quote: Women taking more than 4500 mg RE of total Vitamin A (from food and supplement) daily had a 3.5 times higher risk of giving birth to a child with cranial-neural-crest defects
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1576/16 on Vitamin A (Retinol, Retinyl Acetate, Retinyl Palmitate), final version

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes vitamin A in cosmetics is safe at 0.05% RE in body lotion and 0.3% RE in other leave-on and rinse-off products; no numeric margin of safety is stated because the assessment compares exposure to a human tolerable upper intake level rather than an animal-study margin.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS is of the opinion that vitamin A in cosmetics at the concentrations of 0.05% Retinol Equivalent (RE) in body lotion, and 0.3% RE for other leave-on and rinse-off products is safe.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1639/21, revision of SCCS/1576/16 on Vitamin A, final version

names.note: Brand names are not listed: vitamin A is in many multivitamins and prenatal vitamins, and California lists it only above 10,000 IU a day.

dose.text: In animal studies, ribavirin was teratogenic and embryocidal at doses as low as one twentieth of the recommended human dose, and effects increased with dose.

effects.text: In animal studies only, ribavirin caused malformations of the skull, palate, eye, jaw, limbs, skeleton and gastrointestinal tract; the human registry showed no pattern of birth defects.

other_effects.text: The US label reports reduced survival of fetuses and offspring in animals, and an approximately 21% miscarriage rate in the registry, which it calls insufficient to identify a drug risk.

regulatory.text: The boxed warning on US tobramycin injection labeling states that aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.

regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, tobramycin for injection (Northstar Rx), Boxed Warning

window.text: A CDC systematic review suggests streptomycin-related hearing deficits may also relate to exposures that began in the first trimester during prolonged treatment.
window.quote: The deficits identified may also be related to more pregnancies exposed to streptomycin beginning in the first trimester because of the longitudinal nature of the treatment.
window.source_label: Yu PA et al. Safety of Antimicrobials During Pregnancy: A Systematic Review of Antimicrobials Considered for Treatment and Postexposure Prophylaxis of Plague. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50

dose.text: EMA tobramycin inhalation product information says aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm such as congenital deafness when high systemic concentrations are reached, and systemic exposure after inhalation is very low.
dose.quote: aminoglycosides can cause foetal harm (e.g. congenital deafness) when high systemic concentrations are achieved in a pregnant woman. Systemic exposure following inhalation of TOBI Podhaler is very low
dose.source_label: EMA, TOBI Podhaler (tobramycin inhalation powder) SmPC section 4.6

effects.text: US aminoglycoside labeling reports several cases of total irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy.
effects.quote: Aminoglycoside antibiotics cross the placenta, and there have been several reports of total irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, tobramycin for injection (Northstar Rx), Precautions: Pregnancy Category D

other_effects.text: French tobramycin product information advises against use in pregnancy because of a potential risk of fetal ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and restricts use to serious infections.
other_effects.quote: L'utilisation de ce médicament est déconseillée au cours de la grossesse en raison d'un risque potentiel d'ototoxicité et de néphrotoxicité fœtales. Son utilisation sera strictement limitée aux pathologies infectieuses graves.
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, NEBCINE 100 mg solution injectable (tobramycin), RCP section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: A CDC systematic review reports hearing or vestibular deficits in 18 of 121 children (15%) after prenatal streptomycin exposure, pooled from 2 cohort studies and 2 case series, with no unexposed comparison group given.
absolute_risk.quote: Combined data from 121 prenatal streptomycin exposures in 2 cohort studies and 2 case series evaluated ototoxicity in children; 18/121 (15%) of children had either hearing or vestibular deficits based on audiogram and caloric testing
absolute_risk.source_label: Yu PA et al. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50 (CDC systematic review)

monitoring.text: French tobramycin product information recommends assessing the newborn's hearing (otoacoustic emissions) and kidney function after exposure during pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: Dans le cas d'une exposition à ce médicament en cours de grossesse, une évaluation de la fonction auditive (autoémissions) et rénale du nouveau-né est recommandée.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, NEBCINE 100 mg solution injectable (tobramycin), RCP section 4.6

evidence_base.quote: totaling 27 751 prenatal exposures to amikacin (n = 9), gentamicin (n = 345), plazomicin (n = 0), streptomycin (n = 285), tobramycin (n = 43)

regulatory.text: The US testosterone enanthate label, like the other US androgen labels read, contraindicates androgens in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.quote: Androgens are contraindicated in men with carcinomas of the breast or with known or suspected carcinomas of the prostate and in women who are or may become pregnant.
regulatory.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

window.text: The US label, counting by trimester, says masculinisation of a female fetus is most likely when androgens are given in the first trimester, and its degree is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus.
window.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus and is most likely to occur in the female fetus when the drugs are given in the first trimester.
window.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

dose.text: The US methyltestosterone label says the degree of masculinisation is related to the amount of drug given and the age of the fetus, and it states no threshold dose.
dose.quote: The degree of masculinization is related to the amount of drug given and age of the fetus
dose.source_label: US label, Methitest (methyltestosterone) tablets, Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York, Contraindications, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says androgens given in pregnancy virilise the external genitals of a female fetus, with clitoral enlargement, abnormal vaginal development and genital folds fused into a scrotum-like structure.
effects.quote: When administered to pregnant women, androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus. This virilization includes clitoromegaly, abnormal vaginal development, and fusion of genital folds to form a scrotal-like structure.
effects.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

other_effects.text: In animal studies, the US Xyosted label says testosterone exposure in the womb caused hormonal and behavioural changes in offspring as well as structural impairments of reproductive tissues in both sexes.
other_effects.quote: In animal developmental studies, exposure to testosterone in utero resulted in hormonal and behavioral changes in offspring and structural impairments of reproductive tissues in female and male offspring.
other_effects.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

paternal.text: France's ANSM says pregnant women must avoid all contact with testosterone gel application sites, and a man whose partner is pregnant must be especially careful with the precautions against transfer.
paternal.quote: Les femmes enceintes doivent éviter tout contact avec les sites d'application de ce médicament. En cas de grossesse chez sa partenaire, le patient devra être d'autant plus vigilant quant aux précautions d'utilisation
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Androgel 50 mg gel transdermique en sachet-dose, RCP section 4.4 (Transfert peau à peau)

monitoring.text: The US label says a patient who becomes pregnant while taking androgens should be told of the potential hazard to the fetus, and it names no specific prenatal test or newborn check.
monitoring.quote: If the patient becomes pregnant while taking androgens, she should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The Xyosted label bases the statement that testosterone is teratogenic on animal data and its mechanism of action, and it gives no count of exposed human pregnancies.
evidence_base.quote: Testosterone is teratogenic and may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman based on data from animal studies and its mechanism of action
evidence_base.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

window.text: The EMA assessment places the sensitive period at 21 to 35 days after conception, counted from conception rather than from the last period, when the limbs and major organs form.
window.quote: This sensitive period is 21-35 days after conception, a crucial time for the development of the limbs and major organ systems
window.source_label: EMA CHMP assessment report, Thalidomide Pharmion (now Thalidomide BMS), non-clinical section on embryo-foetal development

dose.text: The current US label says that even a single capsule, of any strength, taken during pregnancy can cause severe birth defects.
dose.quote: Even a single dose [1 capsule (regardless of strength)] taken by a pregnant woman during her pregnancy can cause severe birth defects.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), boxed warning, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v25)

effects.text: Birth defects named in the EU product information include missing or partly missing arms and/or legs (amelia, phocomelia, hemimelia), small ears with blind or absent ear canals, eye defects, heart disease and kidney abnormalities.
effects.quote: ectromelia (amelia, phocomelia, hemimelia) of the upper and/or lower extremities, microtia with abnormality of the external acoustic meatus (blind or absent), middle and internal ear lesions (less frequent), ocular lesions (anophthalmia, microphthalmia), congenital heart disease, renal abnormalities.
effects.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: The EU product information says thalidomide causes severe birth defects at a high frequency, about 30%, and gives no comparison rate.
absolute_risk.quote: Thalidomide is a powerful human teratogen, inducing a high frequency (about 30 %) of severe and live-threatening birth defects
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

before_after.text: EU labelling requires women of childbearing potential to use one effective contraceptive from at least 4 weeks before to at least 4 weeks after treatment, interruptions included, unless committed to absolute, continuous, monthly-confirmed abstinence.
before_after.quote: method of contraception for at least 4 weeks before start of treatment, during treatment, and until at least 4 weeks after thalidomide treatment and even in case of dose interruption unless the patient commits to absolute and continuous abstinence
before_after.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.4 (Pregnancy Prevention Programme, Contraception)

paternal.text: As a precaution, EU labelling requires men to use condoms during treatment, dose interruptions and for at least 7 days after stopping if their partner is pregnant, or could become pregnant without effective contraception.
paternal.quote: as a precaution all male patients must use condoms during treatment, during dose interruption and for at least 7 days following discontinuation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or is of childbearing potential not using effective contraception.
paternal.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.4 (Men)

other_effects.text: The US label reports death at or shortly after birth in about 40% of infants, without saying which infants were counted.
other_effects.quote: Mortality at or shortly after birth has been reported in about 40% of infants.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity, via openFDA (SPL version 25)

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates thalidomide in pregnancy, and in women who could become pregnant unless every condition of its Pregnancy Prevention Programme is met.
regulatory.quote: Thalidomide is contraindicated during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential unless all the conditions of the Pregnancy Prevention Programme are met
regulatory.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6 (see also section 4.3)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs, the EU label says thalidomide must be stopped immediately and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with thalidomide, treatment must be stopped immediately and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

evidence_base.text: The US label gives no count of exposed pregnancies and names oral ingestion as the only maternal exposure known to cause birth defects, with no specific data on risks of skin absorption or inhalation.
evidence_base.quote: Oral ingestion is the only type of maternal THALOMID exposure known to result in drug-associated birth defects. There are no specific data available regarding the reproductive risks of cutaneous absorption or inhalation of THALOMID
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity, via openFDA (SPL version 25)

window.text: A CDC systematic review suggests streptomycin-related hearing deficits may also relate to exposures that began in the first trimester during prolonged treatment.
window.quote: The deficits identified may also be related to more pregnancies exposed to streptomycin beginning in the first trimester because of the longitudinal nature of the treatment.
window.source_label: Yu PA et al. Safety of Antimicrobials During Pregnancy: A Systematic Review of Antimicrobials Considered for Treatment and Postexposure Prophylaxis of Plague. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50

dose.text: EMA tobramycin inhalation product information says aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm such as congenital deafness when high systemic concentrations are reached, and systemic exposure after inhalation is very low.
dose.quote: aminoglycosides can cause foetal harm (e.g. congenital deafness) when high systemic concentrations are achieved in a pregnant woman. Systemic exposure following inhalation of TOBI Podhaler is very low
dose.source_label: EMA, TOBI Podhaler (tobramycin inhalation powder) SmPC section 4.6

effects.text: US aminoglycoside labeling reports several cases of total irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy.
effects.quote: Aminoglycoside antibiotics cross the placenta, and there have been several reports of total irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in children whose mothers received streptomycin during pregnancy.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, tobramycin for injection (Northstar Rx), Precautions: Pregnancy Category D

other_effects.text: French tobramycin product information advises against use in pregnancy because of a potential risk of fetal ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and restricts use to serious infections.
other_effects.quote: L'utilisation de ce médicament est déconseillée au cours de la grossesse en raison d'un risque potentiel d'ototoxicité et de néphrotoxicité fœtales. Son utilisation sera strictement limitée aux pathologies infectieuses graves.
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, NEBCINE 100 mg solution injectable (tobramycin), RCP section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: A CDC systematic review reports hearing or vestibular deficits in 18 of 121 children (15%) after prenatal streptomycin exposure, pooled from 2 cohort studies and 2 case series, with no unexposed comparison group given.
absolute_risk.quote: Combined data from 121 prenatal streptomycin exposures in 2 cohort studies and 2 case series evaluated ototoxicity in children; 18/121 (15%) of children had either hearing or vestibular deficits based on audiogram and caloric testing
absolute_risk.source_label: Yu PA et al. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50 (CDC systematic review)

monitoring.text: French tobramycin product information recommends assessing the newborn's hearing (otoacoustic emissions) and kidney function after exposure during pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: Dans le cas d'une exposition à ce médicament en cours de grossesse, une évaluation de la fonction auditive (autoémissions) et rénale du nouveau-né est recommandée.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, NEBCINE 100 mg solution injectable (tobramycin), RCP section 4.6

evidence_base.text: A CDC systematic review of published studies and case reports counted 9 prenatal exposures to amikacin, 345 to gentamicin, 285 to streptomycin and 43 to tobramycin.
evidence_base.quote: totaling 27 751 prenatal exposures to amikacin (n = 9), gentamicin (n = 345), plazomicin (n = 0), streptomycin (n = 285), tobramycin (n = 43)
evidence_base.source_label: Yu PA et al. Clin Infect Dis 2020;70(Suppl 1):S37-S50 (CDC systematic review, PROSPERO CRD42018095490)
