window.text: The FDA label says the oral clefts linked to topiramate occur in the first trimester, and small-for-age babies were more common when use continued until later in pregnancy.
window.quote: Because of the risk of oral clefts to the fetus, which occur in the first trimester of pregnancy, all women of childbearing potential should be informed of the potential risk to the fetus from exposure to topiramate.
window.source_label: US FDA label, Topamax (Janssen), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Clinical Considerations

dose.text: EMA states that the malformation risk has been reported to rise with dose, and that effects were observed at all doses.
dose.quote: The risk has been reported to be dose dependent; effects were observed in all doses.
dose.source_label: EMA, topiramate Article 31 referral, Annex III (agreed SmPC section 4.6 wording), CMDh position 11 October 2023

effects.text: EMA lists cleft lip or palate, hypospadias and malformations of other body systems, and also reports low birth weight, small size for age and a possible rise in neurodevelopmental disorders.
effects.quote: An increased risk of congenital malformations (particularly cleft lip/palate, hypospadias, and anomalies involving various body systems) following exposure during the first trimester.
effects.source_label: EMA, topiramate Article 31 referral, Annex III (agreed SmPC section 4.6 wording), CMDh position 11 October 2023

absolute_risk.text: In the North American registry, 4.3 in 100 babies exposed to topiramate alone had a major birth defect, against 1.4 in 100 in a group not taking antiseizure medicines.
absolute_risk.quote: The North American Antiepileptic Drug pregnancy registry data for topiramate monotherapy showed an approximate 3-fold higher prevalence of major congenital malformations (4.3%), compared with a reference group not taking AEDs (1.4%).
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, topiramate Article 31 referral, Annex III (agreed SmPC section 4.6 wording), CMDh position 11 October 2023

before_after.text: For women who can become pregnant, the UK regulator requires a negative pregnancy test before starting and highly effective contraception throughout treatment and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose.
before_after.quote: discuss with them the need to use highly effective contraception throughout treatment and for at least four weeks after the last dose of topiramate
before_after.source_label: MHRA Drug Safety Update vol. 17 issue 11, Topiramate (Topamax): introduction of new safety measures, including a Pregnancy Prevention Programme (Advice for prescribers)

other_effects.text: Beyond malformations, EMA says topiramate can cause foetal growth restriction, and some data suggest a higher risk of neurodevelopmental disorders while other data do not.
other_effects.quote: Some data suggest an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children exposed to topiramate in utero, while other data do not suggest such an increased risk
other_effects.source_label: EMA, topiramate Article 31 referral (EMEA/H/A-31/1520), Annex III: agreed product-information wording, CMDh position (SmPC section 4.4)

regulatory.text: ANSM contraindicates topiramate in pregnancy and in women who could conceive without highly effective contraception, with two epilepsy-only exceptions; dispensing to them, pregnant women and girls requires an annual co-signed attestation.
regulatory.quote: Médicament nécessitant une surveillance particulière pendant le traitement : la prescription initiale annuelle nécessite la signature par le médecin et la patiente de l’attestation d’information partagée. La délivrance nécessite la présentation de l’attestation annuelle co-signée.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, RCP EPITOMAX 100 mg comprimé pelliculé (topiramate), sections 4.3 and 4.6 and Conditions de prescription et de délivrance, updated 18/09/2025

monitoring.text: For epilepsy, EMA says that if topiramate is used in pregnancy, the woman should be referred to a specialist for evaluation and counselling, with careful prenatal monitoring.
monitoring.quote: If topiramate is used during pregnancy, the patient should be referred to a specialist for evaluation and counselling regarding the exposed pregnancy. Careful prenatal monitoring should be performed.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, topiramate Article 31 referral (EMEA/H/A-31/1520), Annex III: agreed product-information wording, CMDh position (SmPC section 4.6, indication epilepsy)

evidence_base.text: A 2023 Cochrane review pooled 510 topiramate-exposed children from eight cohort studies and found major malformations in 3.9% of them.
evidence_base.quote: The prevalence of major malformations (any type) in cohort studies for children exposed to topiramate (TPM) (N = 510), based on data from eight studies, was 3.9% (95% CI 2.3 to 6.5).
evidence_base.source_label: Bromley R et al., Monotherapy treatment of epilepsy in pregnancy: congenital malformation outcomes in the child, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023;8:CD010224

window.text: Counted by trimester, the US label says the risk of major structural defects is greatest in the first trimester, while other serious developmental effects can occur throughout pregnancy.
window.quote: The risk of major structural abnormalities is greatest during the first trimester; however, other serious developmental effects can occur with valproate use throughout pregnancy.
window.source_label: US label, Depakote (divalproex sodium), AbbVie, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

dose.text: The US label says the malformation risk rises with dose, but no threshold dose below which there is no risk can be established.
dose.quote: This risk is dose-dependent; however, a threshold dose below which no risk exists cannot be established.
dose.source_label: US label, Depakote (divalproex sodium), AbbVie, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label lists neural tube defects, cardiovascular malformations, oral clefts, craniosynostosis, hypospadias and limb malformations such as clubfoot and polydactyly among major malformations reported after valproate exposure.
effects.quote: The major congenital malformations included cases of neural tube defects, cardiovascular malformations, craniofacial defects (e.g., oral clefts, craniosynostosis), hypospadias, limb malformations (e.g., clubfoot, polydactyly)
effects.source_label: US label, Depakote (divalproex sodium), AbbVie, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Human Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: EMA's patient wording says that about 10 in 100 babies of women taking valproate in pregnancy have birth defects, compared with 2 to 3 in 100 babies of women without epilepsy.
absolute_risk.quote: in women who take valproate around 10 babies in every 100 will have birth defects. This compares to 2 to 3 babies in every 100 born to women who don’t have epilepsy.
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, valproate Article 31 referral EMEA/H/A-31/1454, Annex III (package leaflet wording)

before_after.text: For women able to have children, French product information requires a negative pregnancy test before starting and at regular intervals, uninterrupted effective contraception, and, if pregnancy is planned, every effort to switch before conception.
before_after.quote: qu’elles ne soient pas enceintes (test de grossesse plasmatique d’une sensibilité d’au moins 25 mUI/ml négatif à l’instauration du traitement et à intervalles réguliers pendant le traitement)
before_after.source_label: ANSM, Depakine 500 mg comprimé gastro-résistant, RCP sections 4.4 and 4.6 (base de données publique des médicaments)

paternal.text: As a precaution against a possible neurodevelopmental risk to children, the MHRA advises men to use condoms plus partner contraception, and not to donate sperm, during valproate treatment and for 3 months after stopping.
paternal.quote: as a precaution, recommend that male patients use effective contraception (condoms, plus contraception used by the female sexual partner) throughout the valproate treatment period and for 3 months after stopping valproate
paternal.source_label: MHRA Drug Safety Update, 'Valproate use in men: as a precaution, men and their partners should use effective contraception'
paternal.id: Drug Safety Update volume 18, issue 2, September 2024

other_effects.text: French product information says studies show up to 30 to 40% of preschool children exposed in utero to valproate monotherapy have early developmental delays, such as late speech and walking.
other_effects.quote: Lorsque le valproate est administré en monothérapie, les études menées chez des enfants d'âge préscolaire exposés in utero au valproate montrent que jusqu'à 30 à 40 % d'entre eux présentent des retards de développement dans la petite enfance
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, Depakine 500 mg comprimé gastro-résistant, RCP section 4.6 (base de données publique des médicaments)

regulatory.text: Since a 2018 EU-wide decision, valproate is contraindicated in girls and women able to have children unless a pregnancy prevention programme is followed, and in pregnancy unless, for epilepsy, no other effective treatment exists.
regulatory.quote: Valproate medicines are now therefore contraindicated, i.e. must not be used, in girls and women able to have children unless the terms of a special pregnancy prevention programme are followed.
regulatory.source_label: EMA, valproate and related substances Article 31 referral EMEA/H/A-31/1454, referral page (overview and information for patients and healthcare professionals)

monitoring.text: For exposed pregnancies, French product information requires specialised prenatal monitoring for neural tube and other defects, maternal and newborn clotting tests around birth, and close follow-up of the child's neurodevelopment.
monitoring.quote: une surveillance prénatale spécialisée doit être instaurée en vue de détecter d’éventuelles anomalies touchant le tube neural ou d’autres malformations
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, Depakine 500 mg comprimé gastro-résistant, RCP section 4.6 (base de données publique des médicaments)

evidence_base.text: A 2023 Cochrane systematic review pooled 3,018 valproate-exposed children from 31 cohort studies and 1,364 from six health-record studies, all observational, finding major malformations in 9.8% and 9.7%.
evidence_base.quote: The prevalence of major malformations (any type) in cohort studies for children exposed to valproate (VPA) (N = 3018), based on data from 31 studies, was 9.8% (95% CI 8.1 to 11.9).
evidence_base.source_label: Bromley et al., Monotherapy treatment of epilepsy in pregnancy: congenital malformation outcomes in the child, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023, Results (valproate)

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates vismodegib in pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential who do not comply with the Erivedge Pregnancy Prevention Programme.
regulatory.quote: Erivedge is contraindicated in WCBP who do not comply with the Erivedge Pregnancy Prevention Programme.

window.text: EU assessors expect vismodegib to cause pronounced fetal toxicity throughout pregnancy, given its strong teratogenic potential and the likely importance of hedgehog signalling in later developmental stages.
window.quote: Based on the strong teratogenic potential, and the likely importance of hedgehog signalling also in later developmental stages, vismodegib is expected to exhibit pronounced foetal toxicity throughout the pregnancy
window.source_label: EMA CHMP assessment report Erivedge (vismodegib), non-clinical discussion

dose.text: In rats, the lowest dose tested, 10 mg/kg/day, about 0.2 times human exposure at 150 mg, caused malformations, and doses of 60 mg/kg/day or more caused early resorption of all fetuses.
dose.quote: A dose of 10 mg/kg/day [approximately 0.2 times the human exposure (AUC) at the recommended 150 mg clinical dose] resulted in malformations (including missing and/or fused digits, open perineum and craniofacial anomalies)
dose.source_label: US FDA label Erivedge (vismodegib), via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data

effects.text: In animal species, hedgehog pathway inhibitors such as vismodegib were embryotoxic or teratogenic and can cause severe malformations, including craniofacial anomalies, midline defects and limb defects.
effects.quote: Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (see section 5.1) such as vismodegib, have been demonstrated to be embryotoxic and/or teratogenic in multiple animal species and can cause severe malformations, including craniofacial anomalies, midline defects and limb defects
effects.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.6 Pregnancy

other_effects.text: The EU label says irreversible tooth defects and premature growth-plate closure, seen in rat toxicity studies at clinically relevant exposures, represent risks to post-natal development; no dedicated post-natal study was done.
other_effects.quote: irreversible defects in growing teeth and premature closure of the femoral epiphyseal plate, observed in rat toxicity studies at clinically relevant exposures, represent risks to post-natal development
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Post-natal development

before_after.text: Women of childbearing potential must use two methods, one highly effective plus a barrier, during treatment and for 24 months after the last dose, and test negative within 7 days before starting.
before_after.quote: Female patients must use two methods of recommended contraception including one highly effective method and a barrier method during Erivedge therapy and for 24 months after the final dose
before_after.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.4 Special warnings, Contraception and Pregnancy testing

paternal.text: Because vismodegib is present in semen, the EU label requires men to use a condom, even after vasectomy, during treatment and for 2 months after the final dose.
paternal.quote: male patients must always use a condom (with spermicide, if available), even after a vasectomy, when having sex with a female partner while taking Erivedge
paternal.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.6 Contraception in males and females

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs during treatment, the EU label requires that Erivedge be stopped immediately.

window.text: Malformations were described mostly after exposure between 6 and 9 weeks of pregnancy, counted from the first day of the last period (weeks of amenorrhoea).
window.quote: un syndrome malformatif a été décrit dans environ 4 % à 7 % des grossesses exposées le plus souvent entre 6 et 9 semaines d'aménorrhée.
window.source_label: ANSM, Résumé des Caractéristiques du Produit, COUMADINE 5 mg (warfarine), section 4.6, updated 01/12/2022

dose.text: In small studies of women with mechanical heart valves, foetal adverse events appear to rise with first-trimester warfarin above 5 mg a day, but can also occur at 5 mg or less.
dose.quote: Thus, while it appears that foetal adverse events increase when the dose of warfarin is >5 mg/day, foetal loss and adverse events can occur in women with doses of warfarin ≤5 mg/day.
dose.source_label: D'Souza et al., Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516 (Discussion)

effects.text: ENTIS experts list multiple malformations including an underdeveloped nose, stippled bone ends, skeletal and finger or toe (digital) defects, with reduced growth and facial differences.
effects.quote: Multiple malformations including nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, skeletal and digital. Growth disruption. Facial dysmorphia.
effects.source_label: ENTIS consensus, Bluett-Duncan et al., Birth Defects Res 2025;117(9):e2497, Table 1 (one cell spanning acenocoumarol, phenindione and warfarin)

absolute_risk.text: First-trimester warfarin exposure caused the malformation pattern in about 5% of exposed babies; the label says this is not an adequate basis for comparison with the 2–4% US background rate.
absolute_risk.quote: Exposure to warfarin during the first trimester of pregnancy caused a pattern of congenital malformations in about 5% of exposed offspring.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Warfarin Sodium tablets (Teva), section 8.1 Pregnancy, effective 2025-06-17

before_after.text: The US label asks prescribers to verify pregnancy status before starting warfarin and to advise effective contraception during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose.
before_after.quote: Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 1 month after the final dose of warfarin sodium.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Warfarin Sodium tablets (Teva), section 8.3 Females and Males of Reproductive Potential, effective 2025-06-17

other_effects.text: The US label states that intellectual disability ('mental retardation'), blindness, schizencephaly, microcephaly, hydrocephalus and other adverse outcomes have been reported after warfarin exposure in the second and third trimesters.
other_effects.quote: Mental retardation, blindness, schizencephaly, microcephaly, hydrocephalus, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes have been reported following warfarin exposure during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Warfarin Sodium tablets (Teva), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Fetal/Neonatal Adverse Reactions, effective 2025-06-17

regulatory.text: The US label contraindicates warfarin in pregnancy except for women with mechanical heart valves at high risk of thromboembolism; its boxed warning concerns bleeding, not pregnancy.
regulatory.quote: Warfarin sodium is contraindicated in women who are pregnant except in pregnant women with mechanical heart valves, who are at high risk of thromboembolism
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Warfarin Sodium tablets (Teva), section 4 Contraindications (boxed warning: bleeding risk), effective 2025-06-17

monitoring.text: If Coumadine is used in pregnancy or pregnancy is discovered on treatment, the French label requires specialised prenatal diagnosis by ultrasound, or even MRI, adapted to the period of exposure.
monitoring.quote: la patiente doit être pleinement informée des risques pour le fœtus et un diagnostic prénatal spécialisé (échographique voire IRM) adapté en fonction de la période d'exposition doit être instauré
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, Résumé des Caractéristiques du Produit, COUMADINE 5 mg (warfarine), section 4.6, updated 01/12/2022

evidence_base.text: A 2017 meta-analysis found no randomised trials; 30 non-randomised studies (1,373 pregnancies) used vitamin K antagonists throughout pregnancy in women with mechanical heart valves, all at moderate or high risk of bias.
evidence_base.quote: Of the 30 studies (1373 pregnancies) that reported the use of VKAs throughout pregnancy, 11 (581 pregnancies) used a standard INR target of 2.5–3.5
evidence_base.source_label: D'Souza et al., Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516 (Results)

exposure.why: Lilial was a fragrance ingredient of many cosmetics until the EU banned it in 2022.
exposure.source: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional, SCCS/1591/17

entries.exposure_why: Lilial was a fragrance in cosmetics and detergents until the EU banned it in cosmetics.

limit.text: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902 adds Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Annex II entry 1666 (CAS 80-54-6), to the cosmetics ban list, applying from 1 March 2022.
limit.quote: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. It shall apply from 1 March 2022.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902 (EUR-Lex, read this session)

basis_dose.text: The SCCS sets the NOAEL for developmental toxicity at 4.5 mg/kg bw/day in an extended one-generation reproductive toxicity rat study, revising its earlier 5 mg/kg bw/day figure.
basis_dose.quote: The NOAEL for developmental toxicity in the F1 and F2 progeny was 3 mg/kg bw/d (equivalent to a mean overall oral dose of 4.5 mg/kg bw/d)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

effects.text: The SCCS attributes lower F1 and F2 rat pup body weights, seen at the top dose, to maternal toxicity rather than a specific developmental effect.
effects.quote: based on reduced pup body weights in the F1 and F2 offspring, which were observed at 10 mg/kg bw/d
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

conclusion.text: The SCCS concludes Lilial cannot be considered safe at the proposed fragrance concentrations once aggregate exposure from all product types is summed, giving a margin of safety of about 80 against the 4.5 mg/kg bw/day NOAEL.
conclusion.quote: However, considering the first-tier deterministic aggregate exposure, arising from the use of different product types together, Butylphenyl methylpropional at the proposed concentrations cannot be considered as safe.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

entries.name: Ambrisentan (endothelin receptor antagonist)

sources.label: EMA: pregnancy prevention programme or contraindication for teratogenicity
sources.note: Pulmonary arterial hypertension medicine (Volibris); teratogenic in animals.

papers.title: Inferior vena cava anomalous drainage into the left atrium with severe pulmonary arterial hypertension: a case report and review of management strategies
In brief: Embryotoxicity REMS removal for endothelin receptor antagonists
Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return Presenting in Adults: A Case Series With Review of Literature
Management of pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC C02KX02).

regulatory.text: FDA states that endothelin receptor antagonist medicines are contraindicated in pregnancy because animal studies show they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: Use of ERA medicines is contraindicated in pregnancy. Based on data from animal EFT studies, pregnant patients should not use ERA medicines as they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA, Endothelin Receptor Antagonist REMS Information (content current as of 03/04/2026)

dose.text: In animal studies, ambrisentan caused birth defects in rats and rabbits at exposures 3.5 and 1.7 times those of the 10 mg human daily dose, and lower doses were not studied.
dose.quote: In animal reproduction studies, Letairis was teratogenic in rats and rabbits at doses which resulted in exposures of 3.5 and 1.7 times, respectively, the human dose of 10 mg per day
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

effects.text: In rats and rabbits, ambrisentan caused abnormalities of the lower jaw and palate, heart and great-vessel malformations, and failure of the thymus and thyroid to form.
effects.quote: In both species, there were abnormalities of the lower jaw and hard and soft palate, malformation of the heart and great vessels, and failure of formation of the thymus and thyroid.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, macitentan given from late pregnancy through lactation reduced pup survival and impaired the male offspring's fertility at all doses tested.
other_effects.quote: Administration of macitentan to female rats from late pregnancy through lactation caused reduced pup survival and impairment of the male fertility of the offspring at all dose levels tested.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Opsumit (macitentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal endothelin receptor antagonist use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US ambrisentan label calls for a pregnancy test before starting and advises effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Obtain a pregnancy test prior to initiation of treatment with Letairis. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for one month after discontinuation of treatment with Letairis.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 5.1 Embryo-fetal Toxicity, via openFDA

paternal.text: The EU macitentan label addresses only male fertility, saying ERAs may harm sperm production in men, not risk to a pregnancy fathered by a treated man.
paternal.quote: Decreases in sperm count have been observed in patients taking ERAs. Macitentan, like other ERAs, may have an adverse effect on spermatogenesis in men.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Opsumit (macitentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 (Male fertility)

monitoring.text: EMA recommends monthly pregnancy tests while a woman of childbearing potential takes ambrisentan.
monitoring.quote: Monthly pregnancy tests during treatment with ambrisentan are recommended.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Volibris (ambrisentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: FDA's 2025 decision rested on human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to any ERA, which showed no pattern of malformations like those seen in animals.
evidence_base.quote: based on an evaluation of human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to a drug in the endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) pharmacologic class. These data have not shown a pattern of congenital malformations
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA, supplement approval letter NDA 022081/S-045 (Letairis), removal of the Ambrisentan REMS

sources.label: EMA: pregnancy prevention programme or contraindication for teratogenicity
sources.note: Pulmonary arterial hypertension medicine (Tracleer); teratogenic in animals; monthly pregnancy testing.

jurisdictions.EU / EEA: Authorised; contraindicated in pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential not using reliable contraception.

papers.title: In brief: Embryotoxicity REMS removal for endothelin receptor antagonists
Pregnancy in systemic sclerosis
In Vitro Micropatterned Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Test (µP-hPST) for Morphometric-Based Teratogen Screening

A successful cesarean delivery without fetal or maternal morbidity in an Eisenmenger patient with cor triatriatum sinistrum, double-orifice mitral valve, large ventricular septal defect, and single ventricle who was under long-term bosentan treatment
Congenital right pulmonary artery agenesis with atrial septal defect and pulmonary hypertension

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC C02KX01).

regulatory.text: The US label carries a boxed warning that contraindicates bosentan in pregnancy because, based on animal data, it may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: TRACLEER is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant females based on animal data.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, Boxed Warning (Embryo-Fetal Toxicity), via openFDA

dose.text: In rats, bosentan caused birth defects at blood levels higher than 1.5 times those reached at the human therapeutic dose.
dose.quote: Bosentan has been shown to be teratogenic in rats at plasma levels higher than 1.5 times the plasma concentrations achieved at the therapeutic dose in humans.
dose.source_label: EMA, Tracleer (bosentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data

effects.text: In a rat study, bosentan caused dose-dependent malformations of the head, mouth, face and large blood vessels.
effects.quote: In an embryo-fetal toxicity study in rats, bosentan showed dose-dependent teratogenic effects, including malformations of the head, mouth, face and large blood vessels.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, bosentan increased stillbirths and deaths of newborn pups at oral doses 2 and 10 times the maximum recommended human dose.
other_effects.quote: Bosentan increased stillbirths and pup mortality at oral doses 2 and 10 times the MRHD (on a mg/m 2 basis).
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal ERA use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US label says to exclude pregnancy before starting bosentan and to use effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Females of reproductive potential: Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment. Use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment and for one month after stopping TRACLEER
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, Boxed Warning (highlights), via openFDA

paternal.text: The US label addresses only male fertility, reporting decreased sperm counts in patients and unknown reversibility, not risk to a pregnancy fathered by a treated man.
paternal.quote: Decreased sperm counts have been observed in patients receiving TRACLEER. Based on these findings and findings in animals, TRACLEER may impair fertility in males of reproductive potential. It is not known whether effects on fertility would be reversible
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.3 Females and Males of Reproductive Potential (Infertility, Males), via openFDA

monitoring.text: EMA recommends monthly pregnancy tests during bosentan treatment for early detection, because hormonal contraception may fail and pregnancy can severely worsen pulmonary hypertension.
monitoring.quote: Because of possible hormonal contraception failure during Tracleer treatment, and also bearing in mind the risk that pulmonary hypertension severely deteriorates with pregnancy, monthly pregnancy tests during treatment with Tracleer are recommended to allow early detection of pregnancy.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Tracleer (bosentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: The human evidence rests on postmarketing reports and published literature from decades of ERA use, which have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects but are limited.
evidence_base.quote: Available data from postmarketing reports and published literature over decades of use with endothelin receptor antagonists (ERA) in the same class as TRACLEER have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects; however, these data are limited.
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

limit.text: Dibutyl phthalate has been banned from cosmetic products since Commission Directive 2004/93/EC, now carried as Annex II entry 675 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009.
limit.quote: 675. Dibutyl phthalate (Cas No 84-74-2)
limit.source_label: Commission Directive 2004/93/EC of 21 September 2004 amending Council Directive 76/768/EEC Annexes II and III, fetched directly from the EUR-Lex/Publications Office cellar; carried forward as Annex II entry 675 of the consolidated Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, independently confirmed in that consolidated text

basis_dose.text: The EU risk assessment derived a developmental-toxicity LOAEL of 2 mg/kg bw/day in rats, since effects were still present at the lowest dose tested.
basis_dose.quote: A LOAEL of 2 mg/kg bw/d feed was derived, since the effects were reversible at all dose levels, particularly the lowest dose level (20 mg/kg feed, equivalent to 1.5 to 3 mg/kg bw/day)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCP/1016/06, Opinion on phthalates in cosmetic products (adopted 21 March 2007)

effects.text: In rats, DBP damages developing germ cells in the testis and produces anti-androgenic effects noted in foetuses, per the committee's summary.
effects.quote: In adult rats, the testis is the target. DBP and DEHP have effects on germ cell development/depletion, BBP affects epididymal spermatozoa concentration. Anti-androgenic effects have also been noted in foetal rats.
effects.source_label: SCCP/1016/06, Opinion on phthalates in cosmetic products (adopted 21 March 2007)

conclusion.text: CIR's Expert Panel reaffirmed in 2002, without reopening the 1985 Final Report, that DBP, DMP and DEP remain safe for cosmetic use at present practices and concentrations.
conclusion.quote: the CIR Expert Panel concludes that Dibutyl Phthalate, Dimethyl Phthalate, and Diethyl Phthalate are safe for use in cosmetic products in the present practices of use and concentration
conclusion.source_label: CIR Expert Panel meeting discussion of June 18-19, 2002 (reaffirming, with edited wording, the Panel's 1985 Final Report on Dibutyl, Dimethyl and Diethyl Phthalate), recapped in CIR's 2024 DBP re-review Strategy Memo

papers.title: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension in Corrected Congenital Left Circumflex Artery to Coronary Sinus Fistula: A Case Report and Literature Review
In brief: Embryotoxicity REMS removal for endothelin receptor antagonists

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC C02KX04).

regulatory.text: FDA states that endothelin receptor antagonist medicines are contraindicated in pregnancy because animal studies show they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: Use of ERA medicines is contraindicated in pregnancy. Based on data from animal EFT studies, pregnant patients should not use ERA medicines as they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA, Endothelin Receptor Antagonist REMS Information (content current as of 03/04/2026)

dose.text: In animal studies, ambrisentan caused birth defects in rats and rabbits at exposures 3.5 and 1.7 times those of the 10 mg human daily dose, and lower doses were not studied.
dose.quote: In animal reproduction studies, Letairis was teratogenic in rats and rabbits at doses which resulted in exposures of 3.5 and 1.7 times, respectively, the human dose of 10 mg per day
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

effects.text: In rats and rabbits, ambrisentan caused abnormalities of the lower jaw and palate, heart and great-vessel malformations, and failure of the thymus and thyroid to form.
effects.quote: In both species, there were abnormalities of the lower jaw and hard and soft palate, malformation of the heart and great vessels, and failure of formation of the thymus and thyroid.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, macitentan given from late pregnancy through lactation reduced pup survival and impaired the male offspring's fertility at all doses tested.
other_effects.quote: Administration of macitentan to female rats from late pregnancy through lactation caused reduced pup survival and impairment of the male fertility of the offspring at all dose levels tested.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Opsumit (macitentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal endothelin receptor antagonist use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US ambrisentan label calls for a pregnancy test before starting and advises effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Obtain a pregnancy test prior to initiation of treatment with Letairis. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for one month after discontinuation of treatment with Letairis.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 5.1 Embryo-fetal Toxicity, via openFDA

paternal.text: The EU macitentan label addresses only male fertility, saying ERAs may harm sperm production in men, not risk to a pregnancy fathered by a treated man.
paternal.quote: Decreases in sperm count have been observed in patients taking ERAs. Macitentan, like other ERAs, may have an adverse effect on spermatogenesis in men.

basis_dose.text: SCCS used a developmental-toxicity NOAEL of 55 mg boric acid/kg bw/day (9.6 mg boron/kg bw/day) across rat, mouse and rabbit studies.
basis_dose.quote: A NOAEL for pre-natal effects in all 3 species has been established at 55 mg/kg bw/day (9.6 mg B/kg bw/day).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

effects.text: SCCS reports that boric acid exposure during pregnancy caused decreased fetal body weight and cardiovascular and rib malformations in rats, mice and rabbits.
effects.quote: Exposure to boric acid during pregnancy (given either throughout gestation or only during major organogenesis) resulted in decreased foetal body weight, and foetal cardiovascular and rib malformations in the rat, mouse and rabbit.
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

conclusion.text: SCCS concluded in 2010 that boric acid, borates and tetraborates were safe within Annex III concentration limits, with a margin of safety of 480, before the EU later banned them outright.
conclusion.quote: boric acid, borates and tetraborates are safe when used under the conditions laid down in entry 1a of Annex III.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

entries.exposure_why: It is taken as a medicine, and treatment is how a pregnancy meets it (WHO ATC L04AX06).

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates pomalidomide in pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential unless all conditions of the pregnancy prevention programme are met.
regulatory.quote: Pomalidomide is contraindicated during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential, except when all the conditions for pregnancy prevention have been met (see sections 4.3 and 4.4).
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Pregnancy

window.text: In animal studies, pomalidomide was teratogenic in rats and rabbits when given during the period of major organogenesis.
window.quote: Pomalidomide was found to be teratogenic in both rats and rabbits when administered during the period of major organogenesis.
window.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

dose.text: In rabbits, the developmental no-observed-adverse-effect level lay below 10 mg/kg/day, the lowest dose tested, whose exposure was similar to that from a 4 mg clinical dose.
dose.quote: the developmental NOAEL was < 10 mg/kg/day (AUC24h was 418 ng•h/mL on Gestation Day 19 at this lowest dose tested, which was similar to that obtained from a 4 mg clinical dose)
dose.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

effects.text: In animal studies, pomalidomide caused limb anomalies with unattached or absent digits in rabbits at 250 mg/kg/day, and absent bladder and thyroid in rats at all doses tested.
effects.quote: At 250 mg/kg/day, fetal malformations included limb anomalies (flexed and/or rotated fore- and/or hindlimbs, unattached or absent digit) and associated skeletal malformations
effects.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

other_effects.text: In rabbits, pomalidomide at 100 and 250 mg/kg/day slightly increased post-implantation loss and slightly decreased fetal body weights.
other_effects.quote: At 100 and 250 mg/kg/day, there were slight increases in post-implantation loss and slight decreases in fetal body weights.
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

before_after.text: The EU label requires women of childbearing potential to use effective contraception without interruption from at least 4 weeks before treatment until at least 4 weeks after it ends.
before_after.quote: She understands the need for effective contraception, without interruption, at least 4 weeks before starting treatment, throughout the entire duration of treatment, and at least 4 weeks after the end of treatment
before_after.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.4 Special warnings, Counselling

paternal.text: As a precaution, the EU label asks men taking pomalidomide to use condoms during treatment, dose interruptions and for 7 days after stopping if the partner is pregnant, or fertile without contraception.
paternal.quote: As a precaution, all male patients taking pomalidomide should use condoms throughout treatment duration, during dose interruption and for 7 days after cessation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or of childbearing potential and has no contraception
paternal.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Contraception in males and females

monitoring.text: If a treated woman becomes pregnant, the EU label says to stop treatment and refer her to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with pomalidomide, treatment must be stopped and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: The US label bases its embryo-fetal harm warning on pomalidomide's mechanism of action and on findings from animal studies.
evidence_base.quote: Based on the mechanism of action [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] and findings from animal studies, POMALYST can cause embryo-fetal harm when administered to a pregnant female and is contraindicated during pregnancy
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label Pomalyst (pomalidomide), via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary

effects.source_label: CIR, Safety Assessment of Methacrylate Ester Monomers as Used in Cosmetics (Re-Review, Nov. 2021)

conclusion.text: The CIR Expert Panel reaffirmed its 2005 conclusion that Tetrahydrofurfuryl Methacrylate is safe as used in nail enhancement products when skin contact is avoided, declining to reopen the assessment at its December 2021 meeting.
conclusion.quote: The Panel determined to not reopen this safety assessment on methacrylate ester monomers and reaffirmed the original conclusion.
conclusion.source_label: CIR, Rereview Summary: Methacrylate Ester Monomers, Admin materials for the 160th Expert Panel Meeting, March 7-8 2022 (recounting the December 2021 decision)

exposure.why: Quaternium-15 was a preservative listed in the EU cosmetic ingredient inventory before its ban.
exposure.source: European Commission, CosIng inventory (2016 export)

entries.exposure_why: A formaldehyde-releasing preservative, it has been used in cosmetics and household products.

limit.text: EU law bans Quaternium-15's CMR cis-isomer in cosmetics under Annex II (entries 1385-1386) since Regulation (EU) 2019/831 of 22 May 2019, which deleted its prior 0.2% Annex V preservative allowance.
limit.quote: Quaternium-15 should be deleted from the list of preservatives allowed in cosmetic products in Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 and added to the list of substances prohibited in cosmetic products in Annex II
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/831 of 22 May 2019, recital 6 and Annex entries 1385-1386 (OJ L 137/29-30, 23.5.2019)

basis_dose.text: In Fischer 344 rats dosed by gavage in 1981, the sponsor proposed a NOEL of 5 mg/kg bw/day for maternal and foetal toxicity, which SCCS says should rather be considered a LOAEL.
basis_dose.quote: The applicant deduced a NOEL of 5 mg/kg bw/day for maternal and foetal toxicity.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 3.3.8.2

effects.text: In Fischer 344 rats, cis-CTAC caused fetal eye malformations, mainly microphthalmia and anophthalmia, most frequent at 25 and 75 mg/kg bw/day gavage doses.
effects.quote: The majority of the malformed foetuses exhibited anomalies of the eye, microphthalmia or anophthalmia.
effects.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 3.3.8.2

conclusion.text: SCCS could not establish a reliable NOAEL or calculate a margin of safety, and it judges Quaternium-15's cis-isomer may not be safe for continued cosmetic use.
conclusion.quote: the SCCS considers its continued use in cosmetic products may not be safe for the consumers
conclusion.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 4 Conclusion

limit.text: EU Annex III entry 380 caps Hexyl Salicylate at 2% in hydroalcoholic fragrances, 0.5% in rinse-off products, 0.3% in leave-on products, 0.001% in toothpaste/mouthwash, and allows 0.1% in listed products made for children under 3.
limit.quote: Not to be used in preparations for children under 3 years of age, with the exception of (d) “Toothpaste” and (f).
limit.source_label: European Commission CosIng database, Annex III export (entry 380)

basis_dose.text: SCCS used a rat developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day for salicylic acid, Hexyl Salicylate's hydrolysis product, as a read-across point of departure.
basis_dose.quote: SCCS uses the developmental NOAEL of 0.1% (75 mg/kg bw/day) derived from Tanaka et al. (1973a).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Hexyl Salicylate (SCCS/1658/23), final version of 28 February 2024

effects.text: SCCS bases Hexyl Salicylate's margin-of-safety calculation on teratogenic effects seen in orally dosed rats in the Tanaka 1973 study of its metabolite salicylic acid.
effects.quote: based upon the most sensitive observations in orally dosed rats, of teratogenic effects, in the Tanaka et al. 1973 study
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Hexyl Salicylate (SCCS/1658/23), final version of 28 February 2024

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes Hexyl Salicylate is safe at the Annex III concentrations, citing a systemic margin of safety above 100 despite concerns over potential endocrine-disrupting properties.
conclusion.quote: the SCCS considers Hexyl Salicylate safe when used up to the maximum concentrations as provided in Table 1 of this Opinion.

limit.text: Annex III sets methyl salicylate limits ranging from 0.002% in eye makeup to 2.52% in toothpaste depending on product type, under Regulation (EU) 2023/1545, banned for children under 6 except in toothpaste.
limit.quote: Not to be used in preparations for children under 6 years of age, with the exception of (k) "Toothpaste".
limit.source_label: CosIng — EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III, entry 324 (European Commission, DG GROW)

basis_dose.text: SCCS bases its margin-of-safety calculation for methyl salicylate on a developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day from a three-generation rat study by Collins, 1971.
basis_dose.quote: To assess the risk of MeS by systemic exposure, the SCCS has used the NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/d derived from the 3-generation study in rats by oral route (Collins et al., 1971).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

effects.text: At 150 mg/kg bw/day, methyl salicylate significantly decreased litter size, pup viability, survival and weaning data in the second generation of a three-generation rat study, and decreased pup body weight.
effects.quote: statistically significant decrease of litter size, viability (D0), survival (D4), weaning data in the second generation and decreased pup body weight at 150 mg/kg bw/day
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes methyl salicylate is safe at the dossier's maximum concentrations, with systemic margins of safety above 100 for adults and a lowest aggregate value of 108 for children aged 6-10.
conclusion.quote: For children, considering all products taken individually and also the aggregated exposure, the margin of safety is above 100.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

limit.text: Annex III caps salicylic acid at 3.0% in rinse-off hair products, 2.0% in other leave-on products and 0.5% in body lotion, eye and lip products (Regulation (EU) 2021/850); Annex V separately allows 0.5% as a preservative (Regulation (EU) 2019/1966), both banned for children under 3.

basis_dose.text: SCCS bases its margin-of-safety calculation on a developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day for teratogenicity in Wistar rats, from Tanaka et al. 1973a.
basis_dose.quote: The POD is expressed as a no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) of 75 mg/kg/day relating to the most sensitive toxic endpoint i.e. teratogenicity in the rat as the most sensitive species.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

effects.text: SCCS states salicylic acid's Repr. 2 (H361d) classification rests on developmental toxicity in both rats and monkeys, with teratogenic potency strong in rats and lower in monkeys.
effects.quote: salicylic acid was shown to have teratogenic properties but with species differences in potency: strong in rats and lower in monkeys
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes salicylic acid is safe as a 0.5% preservative and up to 3.0%/2.0% for other uses, citing a probabilistic margin of safety of 195 against the 75 mg/kg bw/day NOAEL.
conclusion.quote: The derived MOS with this scenario is 195 and thus demonstrates the safety of salicylic acid for cosmetics, excluding oral products such as toothpaste and mouthwash.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

limit.text: EU bans silver zinc zeolite generally as reprotoxic category 2 (Annex II, Reg. (EU) 2026/909, 28 April 2026), except up to 1% with silver capped at 2.5% in deodorant spray and powder foundation (Annex V).
limit.quote: the silver content in Ammonium Silver Zinc Aluminium Silicate must not exceed 2,5 %.
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex V export (entry 61) and Annex II export (entry 1597), citing Regulation (EU) 2026/909

basis_dose.text: SCCS references a rat two-generation study (Schroeder 2002) using oral gavage doses of 200, 700, and 2000 mg/kg bw/day; offspring heart enlargement, the finding used for developmental classification, appeared at the mid and high doses.
basis_dose.quote: performed with oral gavage doses of 200, 700, 2000 mg/kg bw/day in Rats (Schroeder 2002)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 3.4.5.1 Fertility and reproduction toxicity (dose levels; the heart-enlargement finding is discussed in the following section 3.4.5.2 Developmental Toxicity, citing the same study)

effects.text: In rats, silver zinc zeolite enlarged the heart in F2 pups at the mid dose and in F1 pups at the high dose, alongside maternal toxicity.
effects.quote: the enlargement of hearts reported at the mid dose in F2 pups (5/27 males and 4/26 females)
effects.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 3.4.5.2

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes silver zinc zeolite with up to 2.5% silver is safe at 1% in spray deodorant and powder foundation, with margins of safety of 109 to 3570 depending on exposure route.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS considers that Silver Zinc Zeolite (CAS No. 130328-20-0) incorporating a maximum silver content of 2.5% is safe in spray deodorant and powder foundation when used at the proposed concentration of 1%.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 4 Conclusion

exposure_method: Hand-curated exposure tags for the teratogens register, read by tools/enrich-teratogens-exposure.py. A tag says how a pregnancy meets the substance at a dose that matters. Keys are an entry's name, or the start of it when that matches one entry only. Entries not named here are tagged by rule: Pesticides and biocides when the EU Pesticides Database lists the substance or it has an ISO common name, otherwise Work and industry.
